title: USAG Pressure Washing
description: This requirement is for a non-personal services contract to provide comprehensive pressure washing services across various external facilities, buildings, bridges, and tanks at Fort Bragg, North Carolina, and its surrounding installations including Pope Army Airfield, Camp MacKall, and Linden Oaks. Under this contract, the contractor shall furnish all personnel, equipment, and approved materials necessary to execute scheduled and demand-driven maintenance orders to remove deeply embedded contaminants, dirt, oils, and graffiti. title: Intent to Sole Source- Military Freefall Currency Training Support
description: Notice of Intent to Sole Source. This is not a solicitation, and quotes are not being accepted at this time. Additionally, this posting serves as publicizing of requirement as well as notice of intent to sole-source. The 304th Rescue Squadron (304 RQS) requires integrated commercial contractor support to conduct an advanced Military Freefall (MFF) Currency and Mission Rehearsal Training Event. This event will enable the squadron to maintain combat-effective Guardian Angel (GA) / Pararescue (PJ) operators through specialized parachute insertion, jumpmaster procedures, canopy control, precision landing, high-altitude low-opening (HALO) and high-altitude high-opening (HAHO) operations, combat equipment integration, Military Tandem and Tethered Bundle (MTTB) employment, and night tactical full mission profiles in support of worldwide Personnel Recovery (PR) and combat search and rescue taskings. Breakout of individual requirements:? - Six (6) calendar days of dedicated facility access (5�10 December 2026), including classroom, briefing/debrief space, secure military parachute storage, and designated rigging loft. - Four (4) operational jump days (6�9 December 2026) providing eight (8) billable blade hours utilizing an airworthy, properly authorized rear-ramp turboprop aircraft (Short SC.7 Skyvan) capable of supporting aft-cargo exits, combat equipment, and live tethered bundle deployments. - Seven (7) FAA-certificated parachute rigging personnel dedicated exclusively on each of the four (4) scheduled jump days (28 rigger-days total) to maintain continuous packing and rapid cycle times for military ram-air parachute systems. - Four (4) jump days of dedicated drop zone management, communications, and emergency response coordination at the primary airfield drop zone. - One (1) integrated practical refresher event, including safety checks, specialized equipment delivery, and instructor observation/debrief. - Two (2) days of authorized access and logistics support to an adjacent, austere desert landing zone for tactical MTTB, off-field recovery, and Night Full Mission Profiles. - Two (2) days of mission scenario setup, tactical rehearsal coordination, and night operations support (planned for 8�9 December 2026). - Scalable support for up to thirty (30) Government-designated military operators. All responsible sources may identify their interest and provide capability statements in response to this notice. Responses received within the identified posting period will be considered by the Government. A determination by the Government not to compete the proposed contract based upon responses received is solely at the discretion of the Government. Moreover, approval of any source is required to be awarded a contract by the government, and 355 CONS will not delay award while source approval is pending. The time required for approval of a new source is normally such that an award cannot be delayed pending approval of a new source.? See documentation attached to this notice for additional requirements information.

title: 13A Dredge Material Containment Area (DMCA) Dike Raising and Weir Improvements
description: This is a Sources Sought/Request for Information Only. This is not a Solicitation Annoucement, nor is it a Request for Proposal.. This does not obligate the Government in any contract award. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Savannah District is issuing the sources sought synopsis as a means of conducting market research to identify parties having an interest in and the resources to support the requirements as stated in the scope of work. The results of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned to this procurement is 237990 - Dredging and Surface Clean Up Activities) with a size standard of $37,000,000.00. The Product Service Code is Z1KF - Maintenance of Dredging Facilities. Savannah Harbor is located at Savannah on the northern coast of Georgia / southern coast of South Carolina in Chatham and Jasper Counties, respectively. The Savannah River is the line of demarcation separating Georgia from South Carolina. Savannah Harbor Dredge Material Containment Area (DMCA) 13A, located along and to the north of the Savannah River North Channel across from Elba Island, lies in Jasper County, South Carolina. The area is one of nine confined dredge material containment areas used for dredging the Savannah River channel. The containment area is roughly 1,380 acres in size and parallels the Savannah River beginning at approximate channel station 48+000 and extending south-west to channel station 58+000 and then along the Back River Channel from station 0+000 to about station 6+500.DMCA 13A is located between DMCA 12A and DMCA 13B. Dikes have been constructed around the entire perimeter of this area for confined storage of dredging materials. Although the area has not always had dikes, it has received dredged materials from the Savannah River throughout the 1900�s. The disposal area is drained using a series of water control structures (weirs). The six weirs are located along the backside of DMCA 13A and empty into the marsh. Two of the six weirs are blanked off. The dikes are periodically raised as needed to increase capacity for dredge spoils. Savannah Harbor DMCA 13A will be used primarily for disposal of the O&M maintenance dredging materials that will be excavated during dredging of the Savannah River. In order to safely contain these materials, the capacity of DMCA 13A needs to be increased and improvements to the water control outlets need to be made. The Scope of Work for this project consists of raising the DMCA 13A perimeter back dike, repairs and modifications to four of the six existing weir/water control structures across the back (marsh-side) dike, and the expansion of the bird island. The existing back dike currently spans a length of approximately 10,600 feet and has a crest elevation of approximately 46 feet MLLW. After extending the interior counterweight, the back dike will be raised to a uniform crest elevation of 52 feet MLLW to gain additional capacity for containment of Savannah Harbor dredged material. The existing 13A/13B cross dike currently spans a length of approximately 2,500 feet and has a crest elevation ranging from about 46 to 51 feet MLLW. After extending the interior counterweight for the span, the cross dike will be raised to a crest elevation that varies from 52 feet MLLW in the back to an elevation of 57 feet MLLW at the front. The existing 13A/12A cross dike currently spans a length of approximately 4,800 feet and has a crest elevation ranging from about 52 to 55 feet MLLW. The cross dike will be raised to a crest elevation that varies from 52 feet MLLW in the back to an elevation of 57 feet MLLW at the front. The existing front dike currently spans a length of approximately 16,200 feet and has a crest elevation ranging from about 51 to 52 feet MLLW. The front dike will be raised to a uniform crest elevation of 57 feet MLLW. The fill material for raising the dikes will be obtained from the interior of DMCA 13A. Repairs and modifications to the existing weirs will involve temporary removal, replacement of corroded steel, reinforcement of the outfall stub, the addition of a new bonneted knife gate valves, a new larger weir platform, a catwalk extension, and re-installation on a new slab foundation. The Period of Performance is 540 days from Notice to Proceed. If you are interested in this project and/or your organization has the potential capacity to perform these services, please submit the following to the Point of Contact listed below: 1. Name and Address of Your Firm 2. Point of Contact (Name/Phone/Email) 3. Company Website 4. Unique Entity ID 5. Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE code (https://cage.dla.mil) 6. Business Size, to include designation as HUBZone, 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business (SOB), Woman-Owned Business, and Large Business. The Government must be able to verify SBA certification of HUBZone, 8(a), and SOB via the System for Award Management (SAM) (https://www.sam.gov/) and the Small Business Dynamic Search (https://dsbs.sba .gov /sea rch/dsp _dsbs.cfm) \ 7. Bonding capability for your firm in terms of single and aggregated bonding. In addition, please answer the Sources Sought Questions which are attached to this notice.

title: Solid-State Energy Conversion from Heat to Electricity Request for Information (RFI)
description: The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) Defense Sciences Office (DSO) is requesting information on the current state of the art and technological limitations of solid-state direct thermal-to-electric energy conversion technologies. We define solid state energy conversion as systems that convert a temperature differential directly into electrical energy without utilizing mechanical moving parts (e.g., pistons, turbines, or rotary alternators). This RFI seeks to identify the best possible solid state heat engine performance across a wide operating temperature range, factors that limit performance, and the most attractive use cases if these highly efficient solid state heat engines could be made today. This survey of limits, challenges and use cases will identify opportunities for research and development to inform potential program(s) in this area.

title: APN-AEC11 SOURCE CONTROL (DESIGN BID BUILD) 19 WING, CFB COMOX, LAZO, BC
description: ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE AEC11 Source control (design bid build) 19 wing, CFB Comox, Lazo, BC (with security requirements) 1. PURPOSE OF THIS ADVANCE PROCUREMENT NOTICE This is not a bid solicitation nor a request for proposals. In the context of the major investments announced by the Government and to foster a proactive partnership with industry, DCC is issuing this Advance Procurement Notice (APN) to inform contractors of an upcoming contract opportunity at 19 Wing, CFB Comox, Lazo, BC. The purpose of this APN is to allow contractors to assess their capacity and interest in participating, and to prepare adequately for the potential solicitation process. This is a preliminary notice regarding a potential contract, which includes security requirements. The purpose of this APN is to allow interested contractors to initiate, if required, the sponsorship process to obtain the necessary clearances or security clearances (if applicable). Please note that there is no guarantee that this contract will proceed or that security clearances will be granted within the anticipated timelines or at all as part of the sponsorship process. Please note that this project may include Indigenous businesses participation component in accordance with the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business (PSIB). 2. DESCRIPTION OF THE PROJECT AND SERVICES It is anticipated that the following solicitation will proceed as noted in the table below. This is conditional on the contract receiving approval to proceed from DND. APN or Contract Number: 87758 Approximate Estimate: $9,300,000 Anticipated Posting: January 2027 Description: Remediation of PFAS-impacted soils at CFB Comox through in-situ soil mixing (chemical) and stabilization, selective excavation, off-site disposal, drainage improvements, and site restoration. The work is located within a former detonation and training area and is subject to UXO risk, environmental protection requirements, and tight seasonal construction windows. Construction will be completed in two distinct phases due to schedule constraints, UXO sequencing, and constructability considerations. 3. CONTRACT AWARD AND ANTICIPATED SECURITY REQUIREMENTS To be eligible for contract award, a proponent will be required to, among other things, actively hold or obtain all required security clearance(s) prior to the date of the award, as further detailed in the solicitation documents. The anticipated security clearance level for this contract is Designated Organization Screening (DOS). 4. Industrial Security Program Sponsorship Defence Construction Canada (DCC) is providing contractors early access to the security clearance application process through sponsorship under its Industrial Security Program (ISP). Accordingly, contractors that intend to submit a proposal for this project and that do not actively hold the above identified security clearance(s) should begin forthwith the security clearance application process by applying through DCC’s ISP. Under this program, DCC may, at its entire discretion, provide preliminary assistance to all the potential proponents with their respective security clearance sponsorship process. To begin the security clearance sponsorship process, please submit a sponsorship request application to DCC by following the steps identified on DCC’s website at: https://www.dcc-cdc.gc.ca/industry/security-requirements. In their sponsorship request application to DCC, contractors are asked to quote the following information, among other things: Advance Procurement Notice (APN) number, as identified in Section 2 of this APN; and Level of clearance requested to be sponsored, as identified in Section 3 of this APN. 5. Sponsorship Process Upon receipt, DCC will review the sponsorship request application and will communicate directly with the contractors to provide assistance for the completion of the sponsorship request packages. Once DCC has determined, at its entire discretion, that a contractor: has started the sponsorship process prior to the solicitation being advertised on MERX, has met all the material requirements of the sponsorship request package prior to the closing date indicated in the solicitation, and has submitted a proposal.   DCC will send the documents to the Public Services and Procurement Canada’s (PSPC) Contract Security Program (CSP). Note – Contractors that do not submit a proposal will not be able to attain clearance through this sponsorship process. Following receipt of the sponsorship request package, the CSP will communicate directly with the proponent or tenderer regarding any further steps or actions to be undertaken or the status of the sponsorship request package processing. At such time, the proponent will need to promptly cooperate with CSP to ensure that the process is completed as soon as possible. 6. Questions Any questions pertaining to the sponsoring process through the ISP can be addressed to: Telephone Number: (613) 998-8974; or Email address: ISP.Sponsorship@dcc-cdc.gc.ca Any questions relating to this Advance Procurement Notice can be addressed to: Sarah Kinnon Coordinator, Contract Services Defence Construction Canada (236) 255-1745 Sarah.kinnon@dcc-cdc.gc.ca 7. Disclaimer DCC is only providing assistance, at its entire discretion, for the above stated sponsorship process  and does not provide any representations  or guarantees that a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application forwarded by DCC to the CSP will be successful or result in the granting of the requested security clearance(s) by the CSP. At all times, the processing of a sponsorship request package or a security clearance application is subject to the respective terms, conditions, and timelines of DCC’s ISP sponsorship process and the CSP security clearance granting process. By applying to either of the aforementioned processes, the proponent agrees to bear any fees and risks associated with: (i) the completeness or accuracy, or lack thereof, of its application or related documents submitted under or in connection with either said processes, and (ii) the timeliness, or lack thereof, of any processing or granting of security clearance(s) under or in connection with either said processes. Notwithstanding anything else stated above, DCC shall in no event be liable to the proponent for any direct, indirect, incidental, special, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages arising out or in connection with the above stated sBidding and Documents are available on http://www.merx.com. title: Canadian Defence Academy Research Paper: Understanding Resilience in the Canadian Armed Forces: A Multi-Level Framework
description: This Statement of Work (SOW) defines the scope, deliverables, and requirements for research examining resilience across multiple levels of analysis to inform understandings of resilience as a component of military effectiveness, readiness, adaptation, and preparedness to inform updated methods and approaches supporting CAF professional development. The National Security Institute seeks an academic analysis of resilience concepts and frameworks to support professional military education (PME), professional development (PD), and leader development activities by improving understanding of the relationship between individual, organizational, institutional, and societal resilience.

title: Canadian Defence Academy Research Paper - National Resilience and Whole-of-Society Defence: Nordic Approaches and Implications for the CAF
description: This Statement of Work (SOW) defines the scope, deliverables, and requirements for researching national resilience and whole-of-society approaches to security and defence among selected Nordic allies to inform Professional Military Education (PME) and Professional Development (PD). The National Security Institute seeks an academic assessment of national resilience concepts, structures, and practices to improve understanding of how military organizations contribute to broader societal resilience and preparedness.

title: Canadian Defence Academy Research Paper: Cognitive Resilience and Cognitive Superiority in the CAF Context
description: This Statement of Work (SOW) defines the scope, deliverables, and requirements for examining cognitive resilience and cognitive superiority as components of military effectiveness, decision-making, adaptation, and leader development to inform Professional Military Education (PME) and Professional Development (PD). The National Security Institute seeks an academic assessment of cognitive resilience and cognitive superiority concepts to support PME, PD, and leader development initiatives across the Defence Team.

title: Canadian Defence Academy Research Paper - Hybrid Threats, National Resilience, and Whole-of-Society Understanding
description: This Statement of Work (SOW) defines the scope, deliverables, and requirements for examining how governments, military organizations, and societies understand and assess hybrid threats through a whole-of-society lens to inform Professional Military Education (PME) and Professional Development (PD). The National Security Institute seeks an academic analysis of hybrid threats and whole-of-society approaches to support PME, PD, and leader development activities focused on resilience, preparedness, and strategic understanding.

title: Canadian Defence Academy Research Paper - Cognitive Warfare, Disinformation, and Defence Team Resilience
description: This Statement of Work (SOW) defines the scope, deliverables, and requirements for examining cognitive warfare, disinformation, and influence activities affecting military personnel, defence institutions, and broader society to inform Professional Military Education (PME) and Professional Development (PD). The National Security Institute seeks an analysis of cognitive warfare and information-based threats to support PME, PD, and leader development activities focused on strengthening Defence Team resilience.

title: Ireland – Real estate agency services on a fee or contract basis – Real Estate Consultancy Services Frameworks for Public Transport, Roads, Greenways and Active Travel Projects
description: Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII) intends to establish four-year multi-supplier Real Estate Consultancy Services Frameworks (Lot 1 and 2) to provide a broad range of property, valuation, land acquisition, compensation, estate management, development, regeneration, and related advisory services in support of its infrastructure programmes and corporate property requirements. This competition will comprise of two lots: Lot 1 – Public Transport and Corporate Services This Lot will provide multi-disciplinary real estate consultancy services to support TII's public transport programmes and corporate property portfolio. Public transport projects include light rail, metro and other transport infrastructure projects delivered by TII under its remit from the National Transport Authority. The Framework will be available to TII and any statutory delivery body established for the delivery of MetroLink. Key services include: Property acquisition, disposal and leasing Valuation and compensation advice CPO support services Property negotiations and stakeholder engagement Estate and asset management Development and regeneration advice Rating and taxation services Facilities management Expert witness and dispute resolution services Planning, environmental and specialist property advisory services Estimated value: €12.5 million to €15.75 million. Lot 2 – Major and Minor Roads, Greenways and Active Travel This lot will support the planning and delivery of roads, greenway and active travel projects nationwide and will be available to both TII and Local Authorities. Key services include: Land and property valuation Land acquisition and compensation Agricultural and agronomy advice Accommodation works assessments Wayleave and rights-of-way acquisition Stakeholder and landowner negotiations Land cost estimation and risk assessment CPO support and compensation claim management Arbitration and expert witness services Mapping, land transfer and close-out reporting Estimated value: €9.1 million to €12 million.

title: Balfour Beatty - Roads North of the Thames-LTC - Technology Disconnections and Street Lighting Diversions
description: We are inviting expressions of interest from experienced suppliers for Technology Disconnections and Street Lighting Diversions on the Lower Thames Crossing Roads North programme. The works support the Roads North Temporary Diversions (RNoT), including the A13 and M25 temporary diversion routes. Package Scope The package includes, but is not limited to: Technology disconnections, diversions and alteration works on the M25. Street lighting diversions and alterations on the M25, A13, A1089 and associated side roads. Disconnection, relocation, modification and reconnection of street lighting and technology assets. Alterations to lighting feeder pillars, electrical supplies, cabling and associated infrastructure. Alterations and diversions to technology electrical infrastructure (EI). Installation, relocation or replacement of lighting columns, luminaires, cabling and equipment. Testing, inspection, commissioning and certification of completed works. Managing temporary and permanent arrangements to maintain safe operation of affected systems. Producing test certification, commissioning records and as-built information. Coordinating with the Contractor, Design Team and stakeholders to meet programme and design requirements. Suppliers should be able to: Deliver highway technology disconnections, diversions and street lighting works on operational road networks. Undertake electrical isolation, installation, testing and commissioning. Demonstrate experience working safely on live highways, including strategic roads and motorways. Manage interfaces with existing highway technology and lighting infrastructure. Provide robust quality assurance and testing processes. Deliver within challenging programme and traffic management constraints. Work collaboratively with Tier 1 contractors, designers and stakeholders. Experience & Standards We are looking for companies with: Proven experience delivering street lighting diversions and highway technology works on major infrastructure projects. Experience in feeder pillar alterations, circuit modifications, electrical disconnections/reconnections and lighting works. Appropriately qualified personnel for electrical installation, isolation, inspection, testing and commissioning. Strong health, safety, environmental and quality management systems. Experience working within National Highways and/or local authority environments. Ability to meet Lower Thames Crossing requirements relating to sustainability, carbon reduction and social value. We actively welcome expressions of interest from SMEs with the relevant experience and capability. Next Steps If you are interested and would like further information, including pre-qualification requirements and tender timelines, please respond by 23.11.26. Additional information: The Lower Thames Crossing (LTC) is a new road to better connect Essex and Kent through a tunnel beneath the River Thames. Our purpose is to drive a change in how we deliver - connecting people to jobs and businesses to opportunities, leaving a skills legacy for the local community and construction industry, all whilst restoring nature and drawing a new blueprint for low-carbon construction. Our ambition is to deliver the UK's greenest road, and to do the right thing for local communities and the environment. We can only achieve this with the support of our supply chain, and it is therefore critical that for any supplier to be successful in winning work on LTC, they must demonstrate commitments to supporting delivery of our ambitions: • Delivering the works through a 'zero emissions' solution, and not using diesel on site in any plant or machinery. • Supporting us to leave a skills legacy for the local community, by not only recruiting locally, but upskilling your workforce to enable meaningful progression into higher paid higher skilled work. • Helping to facilitate successful opportunities by providing early careers roles, as well as inspiring young people into construction through delivery of STEM engagement.

title: Design-Build Renovation of Building 164, Outdoor Recreation Center, Homestead Air Reserve Base, Florida
description: The Department of the Air Force intends to award a firm-fixed-price design-build construction contract for renovation of the Outdoor Recreation Facility, Building 164, at Homestead Air Reserve Base, Florida. The Contractor shall furnish all labor, supervision, materials, equipment, transportation, design and engineering services, tools, permits, testing, inspections, quality control, warranties, and closeout documentation necessary to complete the work in accordance with the solicitation, Statement of Work, drawings, specifications, and all attachments. The requirement includes design-build services for renovation and improvement of Building 164. Work includes, but is not limited to, preparation of design documents; demolition; roofing and exterior-envelope improvements; doors, windows, exterior walls, and drainage work; interior renovations; mechanical, plumbing, electrical, and lighting work; site improvements; testing; inspections; warranties; and closeout documentation. The solicitation will include a base requirement consisting of Phases 1 and 2 and a separately priced Option 1 for Phase 3. The specific requirements for the base requirement and Option 1 are identified in Section B and the Statement of Work. SITE VISIT: A site visit will be held on 10 November 2026 at 10:00 a.m. Eastern Time. Attendance is strongly encouraged but is not mandatory. Offerors planning to attend shall submit the completed base-access form no later than 5 November 2026 at 10:00 a.m. Eastern Time. At this time, Homestead Air Reserve Base is processing site-visit access requests for United States citizens only. Site-visit directions and additional access information will be provided to approved attendees. Offerors that do not attend the site visit remain responsible for becoming familiar with existing conditions, site access restrictions, facility operations, utility conditions, material-staging limitations, and all other conditions that may affect performance. QUESTIONS: Questions concerning this solicitation shall be submitted in writing to Tahj Guilford at tahj.guilford.2@us.af.mil no later than 13 November 2026 at 10:00 a.m. Eastern Time. Questions received after the stated deadline may not be answered. The Government anticipates posting responses to timely submitted questions on or about 18 November 2026 at 3:00 p.m. Eastern Time. PROPOSAL SUBMISSION: Offerors shall submit proposals electronically to tahj.guilford.2@us.af.mil no later than 23 November 2026 at 12:00 p.m. Eastern Time. Proposals shall be submitted in the format required by Sections L and M of the solicitation. Offerors are responsible for ensuring proposals are received by the Government before the closing date and time. The Government intends to make award without discussions but reserves the right to conduct discussions if determined to be in the Government�s best interest. All amendments to this solicitation will be posted through SAM.gov. Offerors are responsible for monitoring SAM.gov for amendments and acknowledging all amendments with their proposal. title: Service Order Desk
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/ SOURCES SOUGHT FOR SOLUTION BASED CAPABILITY STATEMENTS ONLY. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) - Fort Carson, CO, in coordination with the Directorate of Public Works (DPW), is seeking Solution based capability statement for an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for Market Research purposes. The requirement is to design, integrate, test, deploy, and support a modernized, commercial Service Order Desk Platform. The core objective is to decouple the Service Order Desk from the legacy Base Operations contract, transitioning it into an independent, highly automated, data-transparent, and user-centric platform. Successful solutions must deliver 100% auditable real-time tracking of funds by facility type, establish direct digital pathways with the Army Maintenance Application (ArMA) without manual data re-entry, and prevent premature ticket closures via multi-state tracking and parallel POC notifications.. Security compliance requires deployment in a secure Department of War (DOW) Impact Level 5 (IL5) cloud environment featuring Role-Based Access Control and CAC/SSO integration . Submissions must be Solution Based Capability Statement not exceeding 10 pages and must be submitted by Monday, November 23, 2026, at 10:00 AM MT to Jessica Smith (Jessica.l.smith499.civ@army.mil), Frank Camacho (frank.m.camacho.civ@army.mil), and MAJ Ryan Lee (jong.d.lee2.mil@army.mil) ====A0001==== This amendment formally establishes the deadline for receipt of industry questions. title: Canonsburg-Houston, Pennsylvania, Local Protection Project (LPP) PL84-99 Rehabilitation
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Pittsburgh District, has a project as the Canonsburg-Houston Local Protection Project (LPP) is an authorized federal flood damage reduction project spanning over 20,500 linear feet of channel improvements along Chartiers Creek. Originally constructed by USACE in two phases (Houston unit completed in 1970; Canonsburg unit completed in 1976), operation and maintenance responsibilities were subsequently transferred to Washington County. Severe storm events resulted in substantial damage to the channel embankment along the right bank of Chartiers Creek, including displacement of stone protection and loss of subgrade stabilization. This rehabilitation contract encompasses repair and re-armoring of the degraded channel reach to restore federal project integrity and design conveyance capacity. The work is to be completed within 365 calendar days after written Notice to Proceed (NTP). The Anticipated Construction Cost is between $150,000.00 and $350,000.00. The North American Industrial Classification Code (NAICS) is 237990 - Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction. The Small Business Size Standard is $45,000,000.00. Any resultant award will be for one (1) Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Purchase Order. The anticipated award date is 11 December 2026. The basis of award will be of best value to the Government. Quotes will be evaluated in accordance with (IAW) RFO Part 13 and 36, price and past performance. The Government reserves the right to reject any quotes that are unrealistically low or exceed available funds for this requirement. Information regarding the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers process for settling requests for equitable adjustments and duration goals to achieve definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under construction contracts can be found by going to https://www.usace.army.mil/Strategic-Partnerships/Partnering/mod/129895/details/443/ then scrolling down on right hand side of page by clicking on View FFP Contract Changes Playbook Here.

title: Service Order Desk
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/ SOURCES SOUGHT FOR SOLUTION BASED CAPABILITY STATEMENTS ONLY. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) - Fort Carson, CO, in coordination with the Directorate of Public Works (DPW), is seeking Solution based capability statement for an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for Market Research purposes. The requirement is to design, integrate, test, deploy, and support a modernized, commercial Service Order Desk Platform. The core objective is to decouple the Service Order Desk from the legacy Base Operations contract, transitioning it into an independent, highly automated, data-transparent, and user-centric platform. Successful solutions must deliver 100% auditable real-time tracking of funds by facility type, establish direct digital pathways with the Army Maintenance Application (ArMA) without manual data re-entry, and prevent premature ticket closures via multi-state tracking and parallel POC notifications.. Security compliance requires deployment in a secure Department of War (DOW) Impact Level 5 (IL5) cloud environment featuring Role-Based Access Control and CAC/SSO integration . Submissions must be Solution Based Capability Statement not exceeding 10 pages and must be submitted by Monday, November 23, 2026, at 10:00 AM MT to Jessica Smith (Jessica.l.smith499.civ@army.mil), Frank Camacho (frank.m.camacho.civ@army.mil), and MAJ Ryan Lee (jong.d.lee2.mil@army.mil)

title: Dry Dock Inspection, Repair, Hull Cleaning and Repainting of up to Six Vessels
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers - St. Paul District is seeking contractors to transport, dry dock, water blast/clean, inspect, repair and repaint six (6) vessels - four (4) unpowered barges and two (2) 43 ft push boat/dredge tender motor vessels. The vessels will be picked up at Lock and Dam 7 - La Crescent, MN (UMRM 702.5), moved to the shipyard, and returned to the same location. One of the barges requires deck replacement and significant structural repairs. Both motor vessels (M/V Hooper and M/V Lyon) require non-destructive testing (NDT - i.e. ultrasonic thickness [UT]) of hulls and complete mechanical and running gear inspection and servicing. Contractor will prepare condition reports and itemized cost estimates for all repairs not explicitly stated in SOW. The Government will issue contract modifications to authorize the additional repairs when the requirements and pricing are known. Contractor is not permitted to operate vessels under their own power. This solicitation may result in multiple firm-fixed price contract awards. Offers will be evaluated based on the price per vessel, shipyard capacity, and past performance, with price being the most important consideration. This solicitation is 100% set-aside for small businesses under NAICS 336611, with an SBA size standard of 1,300 employees. This solicitation may result in multiple contract awards, based on the following factors (in order of importance): Price for each vessel, shipyard capacity, past performance. Interested parties are requested to submit any questions through the PIEE module Q and A section. Offerors are requested to submit their quotes through the PIEE module. Stratton VAMC s mission is to provide world-class healthcare for veterans in the capital region and upstate New York. Background /Objective The Stratton VA Medical Center in Albany, New York, is currently seeking a vendor for the inspection and cleaning of two 25,000-gallon domestic cold water storage tanks located on the 14th floor of the Medical Center. These tanks supply the Medical Center's high loop, floors 5 through 14, with potable domestic water. These tanks also provide redundancy for the fire protection system throughout the building. It is the intent of this contract that the U-1 form (Manufacturer's Data Report for Pressure Vessels) be completed and submitted as required by the provisions of the ASME Boiler and Pressure Vessel Code Rules, Section VII, Division 1 Place of Performance Stratton VAMC, Albany, NY; Bldg. 1, 14th floor. Period of Performance Work will take place Monday-Friday. 7 AM to 4 PM Scope of Work The water storage tanks were installed in 1951 and cleaned/inspected in 2024. Tanks are sound and have not caused any issues, such as leaks or corrosion. They are housed inside on the 14th floor and set horizontally off the ground on a concrete cradle. The tanks are supplied with domestic water from the sub-basement via pumps that convey City of Albany municipal water from the street to the tanks. The tanks have a level float system for operational control. Additionally, the tanks are ASME-pressurized vessels, with compressed house air at the top of each tank, regulated to approximately 18 psi. Specific Tasks cleaning and inspection- Contractor will furnish all parts and labor to accomplish the task of File Review: Perform a review of the available equipment files reflecting original design, OEM construction drawings, repair documentation, and inspection records. The file review aims to fully assess the equipment's operational conditions and history. Contractor will furnish all parts and labor to perform an external visual inspection (VT) utilizing trained engineering personnel competent in tank design and damage mechanisms. Inspections shall include, but are not limited to, the shell, welds, heads, nozzles, appurtenances, relief protection, foundation, and coatings. Contractor will furnish all parts and labor to perform a Non-Destructive Testing inspection utilizing ultrasonic thickness testing (UTT) on the external shell as required. This work shall be performed by trained personnel meeting the requirements of the American Society of Non-Destructive Testing SNT-TC-1A. Contractor will furnish all parts and labor to perform an internal (VT) inspection, liner thickness measurements, and spark testing of the glass liner, which shall be provided by a field service technician. Holiday testing will comply with Standard Practice for Discontinuity (Holiday) Testing of Nonconductive Protective Coating on Metallic Substrates, following ANSVAWWA D103-09 Section 12 by reference to the American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM D1562-01) and STI SP001. Contractor will furnish all parts and labor to ensure tanks are clean and free of any debris before putting tanks back in service. Contractor will furnish all parts and labor to perform an evaluation, which includes an executive summary that outlines any conditions that inhibit the proper use and functionality of the equipment being inspected. And provides a comprehensive report with pictures and all documentation ascertained before, during, and after the inspections. The report should include, but not be limited to, the following: UTT data and thickness measurement location (TML) map Graphical representation of shell thickness data Calculated minimum thickness Wastage rates (if previous data is provided) Remaining life expectancies (if previous data is provided) Repair recommendations with criticality ranking Inspection pictures Future inspection inter

The real property assets (The Property) known as Discovery Park, and shown in Exhibit A, are as follows: 1. Approximately 45 Acres of Greenspace: This tract of land lies on the northern extent of the facility and is bounded by Old Gentilly Road (publicly accessible roadway) as well as Mercury, Uranus and Venus Drives, which are interior to the security fencing. The acreage is currently classified as underutilized greenspace. The tract�s frontage to Old Gentilly Road has availability to direct connection with municipal power, potable water and sewer services. These utilities may be established with each respective service carrier. Please see Exhibit B for a listing of municipal resources which may assist in performing diligence for these service agreements. The acreage includes what were previously large sections of parking areas that supported a previously demolished building. These areas are past their useful service life and thus have been considered greenspace for appraisal purposes. 2. Building 351: Building 351 is an approximately 32,000 sf mixed used facility. The building is subdivided into two main areas: formal event space and cafeteria. The building currently is connected to the MAF utility grids. As a result, some determination will need to be made with respect to severing the building from those utilities and re-establishing utility services from the previously mentioned municipal service providers based upon the proposer�s concept of use. This reconfiguration would be made subject to NASA�s approval and terms of use. The Proposer may choose to propose on either asset separately or a combination of the two. NASA shall have the authority to execute either one or multiple leases in the event The Proposer chooses to include a combination of both assets in their submission. NASA intends to utilize Enhanced Use Lease authority as set forth in 51 U.S.C. 20145 as the sole means to enter into a lease(s) for The Property. The Proposer will assume any and all financial responsibilities for operations and maintenance of The Property under such a lease. The terms and conditions in the attached Model Enhanced Use Lease (EUL) generally demonstrate all the Proposer responsibilities including those maintenance and operational parameters. While The Property has existing utilities which serve other portions of the facility, the Proposer should not assume that any existing utilities will be available for use and that any utilities required for development will be at the sole cost of the Proposer. The Property will be available at award in �as is� condition for no less than one ten (10) year base term. title: Service Order Desk
description: THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI)/ SOURCES SOUGHT FOR SOLUTION BASED CAPABILITY STATEMENTS ONLY. THERE IS NO SOLICITATION AT THIS TIME. The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) - Fort Carson, CO, in coordination with the Directorate of Public Works (DPW), is seeking Solution based capability statement for an Other Transaction Authority (OTA) for Market Research purposes. The requirement is to design, integrate, test, deploy, and support a modernized, commercial Service Order Desk Platform. The core objective is to decouple the Service Order Desk from the legacy Base Operations contract, transitioning it into an independent, highly automated, data-transparent, and user-centric platform. Successful solutions must deliver 100% auditable real-time tracking of funds by facility type, establish direct digital pathways with the Army Maintenance Application (ArMA) without manual data re-entry, and prevent premature ticket closures via multi-state tracking and parallel POC notifications.. Security compliance requires deployment in a secure Department of War (DOW) Impact Level 5 (IL5) cloud environment featuring Role-Based Access Control and CAC/SSO integration . Submissions must be Solution Based Capability Statement not exceeding 10 pages and must be submitted by Monday, November 23, 2026, at 10:00 AM MT to Jessica Smith (Jessica.l.smith499.civ@army.mil), Frank Camacho (frank.m.camacho.civ@army.mil), and MAJ Ryan Lee (jong.d.lee2.mil@army.mil) ====A0001==== This amendment formally establishes the deadline for receipt of industry questions. All questions must be submitted no later than Wednesday, November 4, 2026, at 1000 Hours MT. Questions with answers will be posted Tuesday, November 10, 2026 by 1000 Hours MT. ====A0001==== ====A0002==== The amendment is to attach questions and answers. Please see attachment, SOD -RFI OTA - QA (17NOV26) w answers, for answer to all questions recieved within the submission deadline. ====A0002====

title: Dry Dock Inspection, Repair, Hull Cleaning and Repainting of up to Six Vessels
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers - St. Paul District is seeking contractors to transport, dry dock, water blast/clean, inspect, repair and repaint six (6) vessels - four (4) unpowered barges and two (2) 43 ft push boat/dredge tender motor vessels. The vessels will be picked up at Lock and Dam 7 - La Crescent, MN (UMRM 702.5), moved to the shipyard, and returned to the same location. One of the barges requires deck replacement and significant structural repairs. Both motor vessels (M/V Hooper and M/V Lyon) require non-destructive testing (NDT - i.e. ultrasonic thickness [UT]) of hulls and complete mechanical and running gear inspection and servicing. Contractor will prepare condition reports and itemized cost estimates for all repairs not explicitly stated in SOW. The Government will issue contract modifications to authorize the additional repairs when the requirements and pricing are known. Contractor is not permitted to operate vessels under their own power. This solicitation may result in multiple firm-fixed price contract awards. Offers will be evaluated based on the price per vessel, shipyard capacity, and past performance, with price being the most important consideration. This solicitation is 100% set-aside for small businesses under NAICS 336611, with an SBA size standard of 1,300 employees. This solicitation may result in multiple contract awards, based on the following factors (in order of importance): Price for each vessel, shipyard capacity, past performance. Interested parties are requested to submit any questions through the PIEE module Q and A section. Offerors are requested to submit their quotes through the PIEE module. Links to the PIEE module and for PIEE Registration are in the Attachments/Links section.

title: Recycling Services
description: Amendment 0001--Provides Government responses to offeror questions, site visit sign-in sheet, revised PWS references in TE-1 and TE-2, added TE-10, and extended solicitation date. https://piee.eb.mil/sol/xhtml/unauth/search/oppMgmtLink.xhtml?noticeId=W9124M27QA005&noticeType=CombinedSynopsisSolicitation (i)This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with RFO FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number W9124M-27-Q-A005 is issued as a RFQ for Recycling Services for Fort Stewart and Hunter Army Airfield, GA. This acquisition is set-aside for 100% 8(a) small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. (ii) See Solicitation SF 1449 for a list of line-item number(s) and items, quantities, and units of measure. (iii) This is a non-personal services contract to provide recycling services for the U.S. Army Garrison Fort Stewart (FS) and Hunter Army Airfield (HAAF), Georgia. The Contractor shall provide collection services for all recyclable materials from recycling containers at Fort Stewart (FS) AND Hunter Army Airfield (HAAF) and services to process and prepare material for resale through local recycling markets. (iv) Period of Performance: The base period of performance will be from 01 April 2027 to 31 March 2032. This includes a 1-month phase-in period from 01 April 2027 to 30 April 2027, followed by four (4) one-year option periods beginning each 01 April thereafter. Place of Performance: Fort Stewart (FS) and Hunter Army Airfield (HAAF), Georgia. F.O.B. Offers must be submitted electronically through the Solicitation Module of the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) suite at https://piee.eb.mil/. Point of Contact: Contracting Officer: Lacey Turner; lacey.m.turner2.civ@army.mil, Contract Specialist: Soriena Coward; soriena.coward.civ@army.mil. (viii) The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this acquisition is 562920, Recyclable Material Collection Services, with a corresponding Small Business Size Standard of $25M. title: Moodle Workplace License Renewal
description: Air Force Installation Contracting Center (AFICC) 338 ESS, JBSA-Randolph, TX is conducting an acquisition for Moodle Workplace License Renewal. This requirement consists of the Moodle Workplace software license, which provides a highly customizable, enterprise-grade learning management platform (LMS) operating on-premise for up to 1,000,000 active Department of the Air Force (DAF) users; the Kenai Theme, a proprietary user-interface component that delivers the specific visual styling, navigation, and user-experience layout required to maintain operational consistency for the DAF Learning Services Architecture (DLSA)-myLearning system; and Moodle Standard Guaranteed Support, which provides essential manufacturer-authorized, ticket-based help desk assistance (including critical server-level troubleshooting and error diagnosis) that coordinates directly with Peraton�s hosting infrastructure team to guarantee maximum system availability and mission readiness. The contractor shall deliver authentic, manufacturer-authorized Moodle Workplace software licenses, the Kenai user-interface theme, and Standard Support to maintain uninterrupted, scalable operations for the DLSA-myLearning LMS engine serving up to 1,000,000 active users. The commercial COTS product must support enterprise administration, customized branding, reporting, standard content import/export, and seamless integration with government-approved host environments. To ensure platform integrity on the DoDIN, all software components must strictly comply with AFI 17-130 (Air Force Cybersecurity Program Management), meet the evaluation and validation mandates of DoDI 8500.01 and CNSSP-11, and utilize cryptographic modules conforming to FIPS 140-3 standards. Required Line Items: CLIN 0001 � Moodle Workplace License for access to use Moodle Workplace On-Premise for up to 1,000,000 active users (Qty: 1 Each). CLIN 0002 � Kenai Theme: Moodle US, LLC configurable Kenai branding and user-experience theme (Qty: 1 Each). CLIN 0003 � Support Standard Guaranteed Support: Manufacturer-authorized ticket-based help desk support (Qty: 1 Each). Period of Performance (PoP) is 29 November 2026 through 28 November 2027.

title: Intent to Sole-Source - PdMA Corporation MCEmax Motor Circuit Evaluation System
description: This is a notice of intent to sole-source. Notice ID N68520-26-SIMACQ-JC00000-0045, a request for information and capability statements, is being conducted under the authority of RFO FAR 6.302-1 (�Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements�) as the requirement is estimated at $8,500.00. The Government intends to award a sole-source Purchase Order (PO) to PDMA Corporation (75245), as no other source has the requisite knowledge, technical data, capability, experience, special tooling, and test facilities necessary to fulfill the Government's requirements within the required timeframes. The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, facilities, and equipment necessary to perform annual maintenance and technical support services for one (1) Government-owned PdMA Corporation MCEmax motor circuit evaluation system and its associated proprietary software. Deliverables The contractor shall provide the following data and physical deliverables in support of this SOW: All applicable MCEGold software releases, service packs, hotfixes, and firmware updates. Telephone, email, and remote assistance for hardware and software issues. License keys, activation codes, or dongle support as required to maintain software functionality Release notes, user guidance, or known-issue documentation accompanying software updates. Confirmation that the Government-owned asset remains under active OEM maintenance coverage. This notice of intent is NOT a request for competitive proposals. However, in accordance with RFO FAR 6.103(d) any responsible source that believes it can meet this requirement may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. To be considered, capability statements must clearly demonstrate: Written verification and legally binding documentation proving explicit authorization, licensing, or certification from the Original Equipment Manufacturer, PdMA Corporation, demonstrating the source's legal right and technical capability. All responses must be received in writing no later than 23 November 2026 at 01:00 PM EST and must be submitted via email to the contracting point of contract. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct competitive procurement. Capability Statements shall be sent to: Daniel Collins, Daniel.h.collins4.mil@us.navy.mil.

Volpe National Transportation Systems Center (Volpe Center) is providing support to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Facilities Environmental Cleanup (ECU) Program. As part of this effort, a Remedial Action (RA) will be conducted at one facility in the FAA Eastern Service Area (ESA) to remove identified soil contamination. The site requiring remediation for lead- and polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB)-contaminated soils is QPI RCAG � Matawan, NJ (40.370895�,-74.220954�). The FAA�s ECU Program has identified the potential for environmental and human health risks and/or liability associated with the facility above based on prior research, known historic operations and practices, and required cleanup actions. The Contractor shall conduct all work in accordance with Federal, State, and local requirements. Where inconsistencies exist, the Contractor shall follow the most stringent requirement. The Contractor shall submit a draft Remediation and Restoration work plan (Work Plan) (where applicable) within ten (10) business days of the project kick-off meeting that addresses the project requirements below. This task involves the preparation and submission of a draft and final Work Plan. The Work Plan shall detail the technical approach and schedule for conducting all contaminated soil remediation, disposal, and site restoration activities described below. To assist with preparation of the Work Plan, the contractor shall thoroughly review the Government-furnished information (GFI) for pertinent information. The removal quantities and depths in the Preliminary Assessment/Site Investigation and Remedial Investigation reports (if provided) are to be used as a guide along with the estimated total quantities listed in this SOW Section 2.2.2. The Work Plan shall describe methods and procedures for performing soil remediation, disposal, and restoration. Disposal methods must be detailed by the contractor for the site. FAA has consulted a Licensed Site Remediation Professional (LSRP), and the LSRP will select and approve all disposal facilities where waste and debris is to be shipped. Disposal sampling and paperwork is the responsibility of the contractor. Confirmatory sampling has already been conducted at the site. Additionally, the work plan shall also identify any required permits needed to perform the work. Futhermore, components required with the Work Plan are the Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP), which shall include personnel health and safety precautions to be followed. The work plan shall also include a brief Risk Management Plan that identifies major risks and hazards on each site and discusses ways to minimize these risks. Examples include lead-in-soil concentrations above 200 mg/kg (ppm) or PCB-in-soil concentrations above 0.25 mg/kg. See SOW for greater details.

title: Sources Sought: IEE/ISBEE Capability Inquiry � CRNA Services � Turtle Mountain Service Unit, Quentin N. Burdick Memorial Healthcare Facility, Belcourt, ND.
description: Sources Sought: IHS1532109 � CRNA Services � Turtle Mountain Service Unit, Quentin N. Burdick Memorial Healthcare Facility, Belcourt, ND The Indian Health Service (IHS) seeks capability information from Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs), Indian Economic Enterprises (IEEs), small businesses, and other responsible sources for up to two qualified Certified Registered Nurse Anesthetists (CRNAs) at Quentin N. Burdick Memorial Healthcare Facility, Belcourt, North Dakota 58316. Services include inpatient, outpatient, and emergency anesthesia care for patients of all ages within approved scope and facility-granted privileges. Anticipated assignments are fourteen-day blocks, staffed by one CRNA for fourteen days or two CRNAs for seven days each, with usual weekday clinical hours of 7:00 a.m.�3:30 p.m. and scheduled night, weekend, and Federal holiday on-call and call-back coverage. Assignment frequency and coverage between blocks remain under development. Respondents should recommend feasible schedules and identify whether their approach covers assigned blocks only or continuous coverage. IHS anticipates a firm-fixed-price contract for commercial, non-personal healthcare services, priced by Month (MO), including defined clinical and call coverage and associated contractor costs. The tentative start date is February 1, 2027, with a six-month base period and four six-month option periods. Dates and final requirements are subject to change. Services may begin only after award and required onboarding, credentialing, and privileging. The anticipated NAICS code is 621399 � Offices of All Other Miscellaneous Health Practitioners, with a small business size standard of $10 million in average annual receipts, subject to Contracting Officer confirmation. Respondents may recommend alternatives with supporting rationale. Responses will inform acquisition planning, including consideration of a Buy Indian Act set-aside under 25 U.S.C. 47 and applicable HHSAR requirements. No set-aside determination is announced. Review the full Sources Sought Notice, draft Performance Work Statement (PWS), and Quality Assurance Surveillance Plan (QASP) in this SAM.gov notice�s attachments/links. Capability statements should address: Business name, address, UEI, CAGE code if available, SAM.gov registration status, business size under the anticipated NAICS code, socioeconomic status, and contact information. IEE/ISBEE status, if claimed, including the current IHS Indian Economic Enterprise Representation form and identified Tribe(s). Comparable anesthesia staffing experience, including rural or remote coverage. Staffing capacity, provider availability, mobilization lead time, credentialing support, replacement coverage, safe scheduling, and ability to meet the draft PWS and QASP. Applicable contract vehicles and recommended requirement changes. Optional nonbinding, all-inclusive monthly budget estimates identifying coverage days, rotations, coverage between blocks, clinical and call obligations, and base/option price differences. Price alternative approaches separately. Hourly quotations and formal proposals are not requested. Submit responses by November 23, 2026, at noon Central Time to David.Jones@ihs.gov using the subject line: Sources Sought Notice: IHS1532109 � CRNA Services � Belcourt ND Limit responses to ten single-sided pages, including attachments, in Word or PDF, with at least 12-point font, letter-size pages, and one-inch margins. Mark proprietary information. Do not submit patient information, Social Security numbers, banking information, or individual provider health records. This notice is for market research only. It is not a solicitation or Government commitment. Responses are not offers and cannot be accepted for award. Response costs will not be reimbursed, and submission does not guarantee a solicitation or award. Contact: David Jones, Contract Specialist, IHS Great Plains Area, Division of Acquisition Management; David.Jones@ihs.gov.

title: REMEDIATION AND RESTORATION ACTIVITIES
description: Under an Interagency Agreement, the U.S. Department of Transportation John A. Volpe National Transportation Systems Center (Volpe Center) is providing support to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Facilities Environmental Cleanup (ECU) Program. As part of this effort, a Remedial Action (RA) will be conducted at one facility in the FAA Eastern Service Area (ESA) to remove identified soil contamination. The site requiring remediation for lead- and polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB)-contaminated soils is QPI RCAG � Matawan, NJ (40.370895�,-74.220954�). The FAA�s ECU Program has identified the potential for environmental and human health risks and/or liability associated with the facility above based on prior research, known historic operations and practices, and required cleanup actions. The Contractor shall conduct all work in accordance with Federal, State, and local requirements. Where inconsistencies exist, the Contractor shall follow the most stringent requirement. The Contractor shall submit a draft Remediation and Restoration work plan (Work Plan) (where applicable) within ten (10) business days of the project kick-off meeting that addresses the project requirements below. This task involves the preparation and submission of a draft and final Work Plan. The Work Plan shall detail the technical approach and schedule for conducting all contaminated soil remediation, disposal, and site restoration activities described below. To assist with preparation of the Work Plan, the contractor shall thoroughly review the Government-furnished information (GFI) for pertinent information. The removal quantities and depths in the Preliminary Assessment/Site Investigation and Remedial Investigation reports (if provided) are to be used as a guide along with the estimated total quantities listed in this SOW Section 2.2.2. The Work Plan shall describe methods and procedures for performing soil remediation, disposal, and restoration. Disposal methods must be detailed by the contractor for the site. FAA has consulted a Licensed Site Remediation Professional (LSRP), and the LSRP will select and approve all disposal facilities where waste and debris is to be shipped. Disposal sampling and paperwork is the responsibility of the contractor. Confirmatory sampling has already been conducted at the site. Additionally, the work plan shall also identify any required permits needed to perform the work. Futhermore, components required with the Work Plan are the Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP), which shall include personnel health and safety precautions to be followed. The work plan shall also include a brief Risk Management Plan that identifies major risks and hazards on each site and discusses ways to minimize these risks. An outline summarizing the required content of the work plan is Technical Approach (Method and procedures for soil remediation, removal, disposal a. Identification of required work permits and b. Site Safety Health Plan (SSHP). Risk Management Plan a. Identification of major risks and b.Risk mitigation plan. The contractor should expect a 5-business day Volpe Center review period between submission of the Draft Work Plan and receipt of Volpe Center comments. The Volpe Center and the Contractor shall meet to discuss any comments and changes, if necessary. The contractor shall make the changes and submit a Final Work Plan within 5 business days of the receipt of comments. Contaminated Soil Remediation: Preliminary Assessment/Site Investigation (PA/SI) and Remedial Investigation (RI) activities completed between 2020 and 2025 found soils at the below site containing contamination above FAA�s action levels, which are based on U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and/or New Jersey Residential Soil Remediation Standards. Examples include lead-in-soil concentrations above 200 mg/kg (ppm) or PCB-in-soil concentrations above 0.25 mg/kg. See SOW for greater details.

title: INL Serbia Shooting Range Simulator System
description: The International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Section of the Embassy of the United States of America in Serbia supports procurement of a scenario-based laser shooting range system and complementary tactical preparedness and response police training kits to complete new training facilities at University or Criminal Investigation and Police Studies in Belgrade, Serbia. This training solution will provide controlled, analytical training environment needed to assess, document, and translate scenario-based tactical instruction into measurable performance improvements, institutional accountability and long-term learning. SUBSTANTIVE REQUIREMENTS The contractor shall fulfill the following substantive requirements (See Attachment A RFQ/SOW for a complete listing of requirements/quantities): I LASER TRAINING SIMULATOR SYSTEM II SIMULATION TRAINING CENTRE - TRAINING KITS III INSTALLATION/TRAINING � ONSITE INTERNATIONAL Delivery The vendor is responsible for the delivery of all items. The vendor shall consolidate the entire shipment to prevent loss and misdirection. Entire shipment must be consolidated at the origin and shipped consolidated, partial shipments are not accepted by post due to the Serbian customs donation regulations. Entire shipment must be consolidated under one AWB or CMR. Any lost or damaged items during shipment shall be replaced by the contractor upon notification. Packaging and preservation shall be IAW best commercial practices to enable shipment to final destination in Serbia to the address specified (see Attachment A RFQ/SOW), without repacking or incurring damage during shipment and handling. Delivery shall be made FOB Destination as soon as possible but not later than 90 days from the date of contract award. The Contracting Officer will not negotiate with any contractors other than those of the Government�s choice and will not use the formal source selection procedures described in FAR Part 15. The Government may perform a comparative evaluation to select the contractor that provides the best value, considering the evaluation factors below. The Government will consider the following factors when selecting contractors for award. The following factors shall be used to evaluate quotes: 1) Technical Specifications: Quote must meet or exceed required technical specifications. Compliance with all required features (to include realism of the training, system flexibility, and performance-measurement tools). Quote meets warranty term requirements. Quote verifies compliance with all requested equipment/quantities, utilizing Exhibit A, �Technical Specs�. 2) Delivery Timeline. 3) International Deployment Experience and Maintenance/Support Coverage in Europe: The entity demonstrating International Deployment Experience and Maintenance/Support Coverage in Europe. 4) Past Performance: The entity demonstrates relevant past performance in at least three (3) contracts of similar or superior characteristics to those of this project. 5) Price: The overall price will be considered, and the lowest price is favorable.

title: REMEDIATION AND RESTORATION ACTIVITIES
description: Under an Interagency Agreement, the U.S. Department of Transportation John A. Volpe National Transportation Systems Center (Volpe Center) is providing support to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Facilities Environmental Cleanup (ECU) Program. As part of this effort, a Remedial Action (RA) will be conducted at one facility in the FAA Eastern Service Area (ESA) to remove identified soil contamination. The site requiring remediation for lead- and polychlorinated biphenyl (PCB)-contaminated soils is QPI RCAG � Matawan, NJ (40.370895�,-74.220954�). The FAA�s ECU Program has identified the potential for environmental and human health risks and/or liability associated with the facility above based on prior research, known historic operations and practices, and required cleanup actions. The Contractor shall conduct all work in accordance with Federal, State, and local requirements. Where inconsistencies exist, the Contractor shall follow the most stringent requirement. The Contractor shall submit a draft Remediation and Restoration work plan (Work Plan) (where applicable) within ten (10) business days of the project kick-off meeting that addresses the project requirements below. This task involves the preparation and submission of a draft and final Work Plan. The Work Plan shall detail the technical approach and schedule for conducting all contaminated soil remediation, disposal, and site restoration activities described below. To assist with preparation of the Work Plan, the contractor shall thoroughly review the Government-furnished information (GFI) for pertinent information. The removal quantities and depths in the Preliminary Assessment/Site Investigation and Remedial Investigation reports (if provided) are to be used as a guide along with the estimated total quantities listed in this SOW Section 2.2.2. The Work Plan shall describe methods and procedures for performing soil remediation, disposal, and restoration. Disposal methods must be detailed by the contractor for the site. FAA has consulted a Licensed Site Remediation Professional (LSRP), and the LSRP will select and approve all disposal facilities where waste and debris is to be shipped. Disposal sampling and paperwork is the responsibility of the contractor. Confirmatory sampling has already been conducted at the site. Additionally, the work plan shall also identify any required permits needed to perform the work. Futhermore, components required with the Work Plan are the Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP), which shall include personnel health and safety precautions to be followed. The work plan shall also include a brief Risk Management Plan that identifies major risks and hazards on each site and discusses ways to minimize these risks. An outline summarizing the required content of the work plan is Technical Approach (Method and procedures for soil remediation, removal, disposal a. Identification of required work permits and b. Site Safety Health Plan (SSHP). Risk Management Plan a. Identification of major risks and b.Risk mitigation plan. The contractor should expect a 5-business day Volpe Center review period between submission of the Draft Work Plan and receipt of Volpe Center comments. The Volpe Center and the Contractor shall meet to discuss any comments and changes, if necessary. The contractor shall make the changes and submit a Final Work Plan within 5 business days of the receipt of comments. Contaminated Soil Remediation: Preliminary Assessment/Site Investigation (PA/SI) and Remedial Investigation (RI) activities completed between 2020 and 2025 found soils at the below site containing contamination above FAA�s action levels, which are based on U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and/or New Jersey Residential Soil Remediation Standards. Examples include lead-in-soil concentrations above 200 mg/kg (ppm) or PCB-in-soil concentrations above 0.25 mg/kg. See SOW for greater details.
