title: Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Request for Information (RFI) will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this RFI is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the RFP. The following documents are attached to this RFI Notice: Attachment 1: NGTR RFI Performance Requirements - DRAFT Attachment 2: Program and Risk Feedback Matrix The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Industry Day: 1st Quarter FY27 Estimated Draft RFP Release: 3rd Quarter FY 27 Estimated Final RFP Release: 4th Quarter FY 27 Estimated Award Date: 2nd Quarter FY 28 Target Fleet Delivery: Mid-2034 � Production-ready NGTR systems delivered to fleet locations for aircraft installation Primary Place of Performance: Contractor facility and as needed at government test sites and government facilities for meetings with NAVAIR and NSA. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. Have experience in developing and producing UHF and VHF RF radios supporting military and non-military communications waveforms. Has experience in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Have expertise and experience in reducing total life cycle support costs and utilizing predictive maintenance strategies to streamline repair procedures and reduce maintenance downtime. Have experience establishing, maintaining, and documenting a proactive DMSMS (Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages) and obsolescence programs. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing), with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,250 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5821, (Radio and Television Communication Equipment, Airborne). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. Note: FAR 52.219-14 Limitation on Subcontracting requires a small business prime on a Set-Aside to perform at least 50% of the cost of contract performance. Small business primes may now count �first tier subcontracted� work performed by similarly situated entities as if it were performed by the prime itself. To assist in market research and determination of any applicable small business set-aside for this effort, small businesses interested in priming this effort and planning to use �similarly situated entities� to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting, are requested to identify: The name & CAGE Code of the specific firm(s) intending to partner/subcontract Their small business size status under the NAICS that as the prime, you would assign for their workshare. 6.0 SUBMISSION DETAILS To ensure a fair, orderly, and efficient evaluation process, all interested parties must adhere to the following submission guidelines: 6.1 Logistics and Deadlines Response Date: All submissions must be received no later than 2:00 PM EST on 23 November 2026. Questions Deadline: Clarifying questions regarding this RFI must be submitted via email no later than 10 business days prior to the response date. 6.2 Submission Method and Point of Contact (POC) Delivery: Submissions must be sent via Electronic-mail (Email) to the Contract Specialist, Sham Keswani, at sham.v.keswani.civ@us.navy.mil. Subject Line Format: The email subject line must read: NGTR RFI Response - [Company Name]. Inquiries: No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist listed above. 6.3 Format and Structure Instructions Page Limit: Submissions must not exceed ten (10) pages total (excluding the Program and Risk Feedback Matrix in Section 7.0). Page Size & Margins: Standard 8.5 x 11-inch pages with 1-inch margins. Font: Times New Roman, font size of not less than 10 point. Document Type: Adobe PDF format. Classification: No classified information shall be submitted in response to this RFI. 6.4 Required Content Your submission package must include the following structured sections: Cover Page / Company Profile: Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, DUNS/UEI, Business Size Status under NAICS 334220, and designated Points of Contact (POC) including names, phone numbers, and email addresses. Capabilities Statement: A detailed narrative addressing your ability to meet the special requirements and required capabilities outlined in Section 4.0. Program and Risk Feedback: Completed responses to the targeted questions and the structured feedback matrix outlined in Section 7.0. 6.5 Proprietary Data and Information Handling All data received in response to this RFI that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government. Any information or materials provided in response to this RFI Notice will not be returned. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise resulting from responses to this RF

title: Conservation Law Enforcement Office (CLEO) - Fort Carson, Colorado, Vehicle Fleet Aftermarket Parts Upgrades
description: The Government is conducting market research to identify responsible sources capable of providing commercial vehicle aftermarket equipment and professional mechanical and electrical installation services for three (3) 2024 Ram 2500 pickup trucks supporting the U.S. Army Garrison Fort Carson Directorate of Emergency Services (DES). The anticipated requirement is a Firm-Fixed-Price contract with an anticipated performance start date between 2 January 2027 to 1 March 2027. The contractor shall furnish all required personnel, supervision, facilities, tools, equipment, materials, commercial parts, installation hardware, and other resources necessary to complete the vehicle modifications, except for Government-furnished vehicles, front winches, crossover toolboxes, and headache racks. The anticipated scope includes: (1) procurement and installation of three (3) new winch-ready front brush guard bumpers; (2) installation and electrical integration of three (3) Government-furnished 15,500-lb front winches; (3) installation and weather-sealing of three (3) Government-furnished aluminum crossover toolboxes; (4) structural mounting and electrical integration of three (3) Government-furnished headache racks, including 2,000-lb utility winches and spare-tire brackets; and (5) procurement, mounting, balancing, and safety verification of eight (8) new 265/70R17 all-terrain tires on two (2) vehicles, including environmentally responsible disposal of removed tires. The anticipated requirements, including the scope of supply, incidental installation services, performance standards, and Government-furnished equipment, are provided in the attached draft Salient Characteristics document and attached Sources Sought Notice. The attached Salient Characteristics document identifies the minimum physical, functional, mechanical, electrical, and operational characteristics required for the commercial items and associated integration hardware. Contractor needs to be located in the state of Colorado, perferably in the vicinity of Fort Carson and Colorado Springs. The closing date and time for this Sources Sought is Monday, November 23rd, 2026, at 1200pm Mountain Time. title: FDA Scientific & Regulatory Support Services(SRS)
description: This is not a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) only. This SSN is issued solely for market research and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. Further, the SSN does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The FDA is not seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this SSN; all costs associated with responding to this SSN will be solely at the expense of the interested respondents. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if issued. The purpose of this sources sought synopsis is to gain knowledge of potential qualified vendors to include potential 8(a) vendors 8(a) relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code and capable of providing multidisciplinary scientific and regulatory professional services in support of FDA Centers and Offices. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate determinations about potential sources. Project Title: FDA Scientific and Regulatory Support Services (SRS) IDIQ Background/Overview: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is a science-based regulatory agency critically important to the stability of the nation's public health and health care systems. FDA protects and promotes the health and safety of all Americans by enhancing the availability of safe medical products, foods, and animal products, and by promoting innovation that addresses unmet medical and public health needs. FDA decisions must be based on the best available scientific data and employ the best tools and methods available to ensure products meet the highest quality standards, while fostering innovation in the products it regulates. In support of its regulatory mission, FDA conducts scientific research across a broad range of disciplines including vaccines, drug safety, food safety, medical devices, biologics, toxicology, radiological products, and more. FDA's science is increasingly data-centric, complex, and collaborative, involving multidisciplinary groups across its Centers and Offices. Within the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER), the Office of Computational Science (OCS), established under the Office of Translational Sciences, supports the data management, technical, and analytic needs of the regulatory review process. OCS manages and supports analytical tools, data standards, and computing infrastructure that form the backbone of modern regulatory review for medical products. Purpose: The FDA is seeking information from experienced sources in Scientific and Regulatory Support Services as it is contemplating the establishment of a Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) to such services. The FDA�s primary objective for this effect is to obtain Contractor services related to scientific and regulatory support across a broad range of mission requirements. Depending on the requirement, services may support scientific research, regulatory review, clinical and non-clinical analyses, epidemiology and surveillance, scientific data interpretation, laboratory activities, technical writing, training, and scientific program coordination. Instructions for Responses: Your responses to the questions provided below will assist the Government in selecting the appropriate acquisition method. Page limit: Maximum 15 pages (font size Times New Roman 11 or larger). A copy of the company capability statement will also be accepted (but not in place of the responses to the below questions). The anticipated period of performance is a 5-year ordering period. After review of the responses received, a pre-solicitation synopsis and formal solicitation may be published on SAM.gov. In addition to responses to the below questions, each vendor responding to this SSN shall also fill out and provide responses to �Attachment B-Vendor Feedback Form.� The Vendor Feedback Form is not included in the 15-page limit. A copy of the company capability statement will also be accepted (but not in place of the responses to the below questions or the Vendor Feedback Form). Responses to this notice must include company name, address, point of contact, size of business pursuant to the NAICS code, and must respond to the following questions: Is your business a small business under the NAICS code? Is your firm certified under Section 8(a) of the Small Business Act? Included is a draft Statement of Work that is inclusive of the anticipated Task Areas (Attachment A). All interested parties can provide written opinions on the draft Statement of Work. All opinions expressed should focus on strengthening the draft Statement of Work Tasks to ensure industry understands and comprehends the government�s requirements. Business Status Provide the legal business name and address Primary point of contact and the contact information SAM.gov Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) CAGE code Proposed NAICS code and size status Applicable small-business socioeconomic designations (including 8(a), HUBZone, service-disabled veteran-owned, veteran-owned, women-owned, or small disadvantaged business, as applicable) Identify whether the respondent proposes to participate as prime contractor, joint venture, or subcontractor Responses to this notice shall be submitted via e-mail to Amanda Edger, Contract Specialist, at Amanda.Edger@fda.hhs.gov (with a CC: to Ian Weiss, Contracting Officer, at Ian.Weiss@fda.hhs.gov), by November 19, 2026, at 2:00 pm. After a review of the received responses, a pre-solicitation synopsis and formal solicitation may be published on SAM.gov. No solicitation is currently available. This is not a request for proposals and in no way obligates the Government to award any contract. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will not be considered adequate responses to the solicitation, a request to be added to a prospective offerors list, or a request to receive a copy of the solicitation. description: *11/17/2026 Amendment to add Question and Answer document* THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY. The Government is evaluating whether to establish one or more Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) to support recurring, as-needed purchases of commercial uniform items and related services for Mitchell Hall personnel. title: R408--FY27 Lean and High Reliability Organization Transformation Support
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Lean/HRO Transformation Consulting, Training, Coaching, and Implementation Support Orlando VA Healthcare System (OVAHCS) 1. Purpose and Notice Type This Sources Sought Notice is issued solely for market research and acquisition-planning purposes. It is not a solicitation, request for proposal, request for quotation, invitation for bid, or promise to issue a future solicitation. Responses will assist the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) in identifying qualified sources and determining an appropriate acquisition strategy for Lean transformation and High Reliability Organization (HRO) consulting, training, coaching, and implementation support for the Orlando VA Healthcare System (OVAHCS). The Government is particularly interested in the availability and capability of small business concerns, including certified Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) and Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (VOSBs). A response does not create any contractual obligation, and respondents should not submit proposals or pricing offers at this time. 2. Background OVAHCS is assessing industry capability to support an integrated Lean and HRO transformation. OVAHCS has established strategic priorities and has deployed, or is deploying, a Daily Management System (DMS) designed to help leaders, managers, and frontline employees identify, escalate, and resolve problems at the appropriate organizational level. The contemplated support would strengthen leadership behaviors, workforce capability, visual management, tiered accountability, structured problem solving, process improvement, and sustainment. The objective is to embed repeatable improvement practices that advance access, quality, safety, workforce engagement, and operational performance. 3. Applicable NAICS Code The anticipated North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541611 Administrative Management and General Management Consulting Services. Respondents should identify whether this code appropriately represents the principal nature of the contemplated work and recommend an alternative code, with rationale, if applicable. The applicable small business size standard will be identified in any resulting solicitation. 4. Anticipated Acquisition Strategy No acquisition strategy, contract type, ordering structure, period of performance, or set-aside decision has been finalized. The Contracting Officer will consider the results of this market research, applicable statutes and regulations, available contract vehicles, anticipated competition, and the Government s requirements before selecting an approach. For market-research purposes, respondents should describe their ability to perform as a prime contractor, support one or multiple OVAHCS locations, provide the required labor categories, and manage any proposed subcontractors or teaming partners. 5. Organizational Priorities and Potential Measures The contemplated effort is intended to support the following organizational priorities: Improve the efficiency and effectiveness of meetings, committees, and governance processes. Strengthen management accountability and timely resolution of escalated issues. Improve access to timely healthcare services and associated operational flow. Support workforce retention, empowerment, engagement, and improvement capability. Advance a culture of safety for patients, visitors, and the workforce. Potential measures may include meeting and action-item effectiveness; leader rounding and tiered-huddle reliability; issue-resolution time; access, wait-time, throughput, or length-of-stay measures; workforce engagement and retention indicators; improvement-event outcomes; safety-culture indicators; and validated cost savings or cost avoidance. These examples are illustrative and are not final performance requirements. Respondents should describe experience establishing baselines, selecting meaningful outcome and process measures, validating benefits, creating visual-management tools or dashboards, and reporting progress to operational and executive leaders. Respondents should also identify a recommended reporting cadence and explain how they would transition measurement ownership to Government personnel. 6. Anticipated Scope of Services The contractor may be required to provide qualified personnel, methods, tools, and materials to assist OVAHCS leadership, Quality Management, Systems Redesign and Improvement, and other designated stakeholders. Anticipated services may include: Assessing organizational readiness, current-state practices, maturity, risks, and opportunities. Developing or refining an integrated Lean/HRO transformation roadmap and implementation plan aligned with OVAHCS priorities. Coaching executives, managers, improvement professionals, and frontline teams in Lean leadership, HRO principles, DMS, visual management, tiered accountability, leader standard work, and structured problem solving. Designing and delivering role-based training through onsite, virtual, or blended methods, including practical application and knowledge transfer. Planning, facilitating, and following up on rapid-improvement, value-stream, or other process-improvement events. Supporting improvements in access, patient flow, quality, safety, workforce engagement, clinical wait times, and other priority areas. Developing reusable curricula, job aids, templates, standard work, dashboards, and sustainment materials. Measuring implementation progress and outcomes, identifying barriers, and briefing operational and executive leaders. Building internal capability so OVAHCS personnel can independently coach, facilitate, manage, and sustain the improvement system. Expanding and sustaining successful practices beyond initial implementation areas. Respondents should identify any assumptions, dependencies, Government-furnished information, facility access, data, technology, or other support needed to perform these services effectively. 7. Anticipated Key Personnel The final staffing model has not been determined. OVAHCS is considering a scalable team that may include the following labor categories: Executive-Level Lean/HRO Sensei or Transformation Advisor. Gemba/Daily Management System Sensei or Coach. Rapid Improvement Event or Value-Stream Facilitation Sensei. HRO/Patient Safety Subject-Matter Expert. Executive Clinical Lean Coach. Lean Six Sigma instructor or trainer, as required. Respondents should recommend a staffing model, identify which functions may be combined without reducing quality, state the number and availability of personnel in each proposed category, describe the anticipated mix of onsite and virtual support, and explain how continuity would be maintained if key personnel become unavailable. 8. Illustrative Personnel Qualifications The following qualifications are presented to obtain industry feedback and do not constitute final solicitation requirements. Executive-Level Lean/HRO Sensei or Transformation Advisor Substantial experience coaching senior leaders and leading enterprise or healthcare Lean transformations. title: Q517--PHARMACY BENEFITS SERVICES | WICHITA |
description: QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS Q: Please clarify whether prescription drug ingredient costs reimbursed to participating retail pharmacies are considered pass-through costs or included in the 50% limitations on subcontracting calculation, and whether pharmacy dispensing fees are treated differently. A: This procurement is a services contract subject to the limitations on subcontracting requirements in VAAR 852.219-75. Prescription drug ingredient costs reimbursed to participating retail pharmacies are considered pass-through/direct reimbursement costs and are not considered service performance costs for purposes of the 50% subcontracting calculation. Pharmacy dispensing fees, however, are compensation for pharmacy services performed and are included in the limitations on subcontracting analysis unless performed by a similarly situated certified SDVOSB subcontractor. Offerors remain responsible for ensuring compliance with all applicable SBA and VA limitations on subcontracting requirements.

Services are to be performed on-site at FCI McKean. Place of Performance Place of Performance will be located at FCI McKean, 6975 Route 59 Lewis Run, PA 16738. title: Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Request for Information (RFI) will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this RFI is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the RFP. The following documents are attached to this RFI Notice: Attachment 1: NGTR RFI Performance Requirements - DRAFT Attachment 2: Program and Risk Feedback Matrix The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Industry Day: 1st Quarter FY27 Estimated Draft RFP Release: 3rd Quarter FY 27 Estimated Final RFP Release: 4th Quarter FY 27 Estimated Award Date: 2nd Quarter FY 28 Target Fleet Delivery: Mid-2034 � Production-ready NGTR systems delivered to fleet locations for aircraft installation Primary Place of Performance: Contractor facility and as needed at government test sites and government facilities for meetings with NAVAIR and NSA. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. Have experience in developing and producing UHF and VHF RF radios supporting military and non-military communications waveforms. Has experience in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Have expertise and experience in reducing total life cycle support costs and utilizing predictive maintenance strategies to streamline repair procedures and reduce maintenance downtime. Have experience establishing, maintaining, and documenting a proactive DMSMS (Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages) and obsolescence programs. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing), with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,250 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5821, (Radio and Television Communication Equipment, Airborne). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. Note: FAR 52.219-14 Limitation on Subcontracting requires a small business prime on a Set-Aside to perform at least 50% of the cost of contract performance. Small business primes may now count �first tier subcontracted� work performed by similarly situated entities as if it were performed by the prime itself. To assist in market research and determination of any applicable small business set-aside for this effort, small businesses interested in priming this effort and planning to use �similarly situated entities� to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting, are requested to identify: The name & CAGE Code of the specific firm(s) intending to partner/subcontract Their small business size status under the NAICS that as the prime, you would assign for their workshare. 6.0 SUBMISSION DETAILS To ensure a fair, orderly, and efficient evaluation process, all interested parties must adhere to the following submission guidelines: 6.1 Logistics and Deadlines Response Date: All submissions must be received no later than 2:00 PM EST on 23 November 2026. Questions Deadline: Clarifying questions regarding this RFI must be submitted via email no later than 10 business days prior to the response date. 6.2 Submission Method and Point of Contact (POC) Delivery: Submissions must be sent via Electronic-mail (Email) to the Contract Specialist, Sham Keswani, at sham.v.keswani.civ@us.navy.mil. Subject Line Format: The email subject line must read: NGTR RFI Response - [Company Name]. Inquiries: No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist listed above. 6.3 Format and Structure Instructions Page Limit: Submissions must not exceed ten (10) pages total (excluding the Program and Risk Feedback Matrix in Section 7.0). Page Size & Margins: Standard 8.5 x 11-inch pages with 1-inch margins. Font: Times New Roman, font size of not less than 10 point. Document Type: Adobe PDF format. Classification: No classified information shall be submitted in response to this RFI. 6.4 Required Content Your submission package must include the following structured sections: Cover Page / Company Profile: Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, DUNS/UEI, Business Size Status under NAICS 334220, and designated Points of Contact (POC) including names, phone numbers, and email addresses. Capabilities Statement: A detailed narrative addressing your ability to meet the special requirements and required capabilities outlined in Section 4.0. Program and Risk Feedback: Completed responses to the targeted questions and the structured feedback matrix outlined in Section 7.0. 6.5 Proprietary Data and Information Handling All data received in response to this RFI that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government. Any information or materials provided in response to this RFI Notice will not be returned. title: FDA Scientific & Regulatory Support Services(SRS)
description: This is not a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) only. This SSN is issued solely for market research and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. Further, the SSN does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The FDA is not seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this SSN; all costs associated with responding to this SSN will be solely at the expense of the interested respondents. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if issued. The purpose of this sources sought synopsis is to gain knowledge of potential qualified vendors to include potential 8(a) vendors 8(a) relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code and capable of providing multidisciplinary scientific and regulatory professional services in support of FDA Centers and Offices. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate determinations about potential sources. Project Title: FDA Scientific and Regulatory Support Services (SRS) IDIQ Background/Overview: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is a science-based regulatory agency critically important to the stability of the nation's public health and health care systems. FDA protects and promotes the health and safety of all Americans by enhancing the availability of safe medical products, foods, and animal products, and by promoting innovation that addresses unmet medical and public health needs. FDA decisions must be based on the best available scientific data and employ the best tools and methods available to ensure products meet the highest quality standards, while fostering innovation in the products it regulates. In support of its regulatory mission, FDA conducts scientific research across a broad range of disciplines including vaccines, drug safety, food safety, medical devices, biologics, toxicology, radiological products, and more. FDA's science is increasingly data-centric, complex, and collaborative, involving multidisciplinary groups across its Centers and Offices. Within the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER), the Office of Computational Science (OCS), established under the Office of Translational Sciences, supports the data management, technical, and analytic needs of the regulatory review process. OCS manages and supports analytical tools, data standards, and computing infrastructure that form the backbone of modern regulatory review for medical products. Purpose: The FDA is seeking information from experienced sources in Scientific and Regulatory Support Services as it is contemplating the establishment of a Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) to such services. The FDA�s primary objective for this effect is to obtain Contractor services related to scientific and regulatory support across a broad range of mission requirements. Depending on the requirement, services may support scientific research, regulatory review, clinical and non-clinical analyses, epidemiology and surveillance, scientific data interpretation, laboratory activities, technical writing, training, and scientific program coordination. Objectives: The objective of the contemplated SRS acquisition is to provide FDA with responsive, high-quality scientific and regulatory support across a broad range of mission requirements. Depending on the task order, services may support scientific research, regulatory review, clinical and nonclinical analyses, epidemiology and surveillance, scientific data interpretation, laboratory activities, technical writing, training, and scientific program coordination. The Government is interested in sources capable of providing the scientific depth and operational capacity needed to: Conduct scientifically sound analyses and prepare defensible, traceable technical products supporting FDA review and public-health decisions. Provide qualified personnel across multiple scientific and regulatory disciplines, including specialized and emerging areas. Support clinical and nonclinical study-data review, standardized scientific datasets, statistical computing, data fitness, quality assessment, and interpretation. Respond to multiple simultaneous task orders, changing priorities, time-sensitive scientific questions, and evolving requirements across FDA organizations. Maintain scientific quality, data integrity, documentation, confidentiality, and continuity of performance. Deliver effective scientific training, technical writing, knowledge transfer, and program-management support tied directly to scientific and regulatory missions. Project Requirements: The following descriptions are illustrative of the types of services that may be ordered. They are provided to inform industry responses and do not establish final task-order requirements. Each task order would define its own objectives, tasks, deliverables, performance expectations, staffing qualifications, and period of performance. Scientific Research and Regulatory Review Support: Support scientific investigations, literature and evidence reviews, research planning, study design, methodological assessments, scientific consultations, and technical analyses relevant to FDA-regulated products. Prepare scientific assessments, briefing materials, review support documentation, and other products that allow Government scientists and reviewers to evaluate scientific evidence and communicate findings. Provide subject-matter expertise to address complex or emerging regulatory science questions. Clinical and Nonclinical Study-Data Review and Analysis: Support the scientific review of clinical and nonclinical datasets submitted for regulatory purposes, including data fitness and completeness assessments, exploratory safety analyses, descriptive and inferential statistical analyses, and preparation of tables, listings, figures, and visualizations. Experience with standards such as CDISC SDTM, ADaM, and SEND may be relevant. The RRS BPA describes review-oriented services that assess study data and produce analyses for FDA reviewers; SRS would focus on the scientific and analytical performance of those services rather than maintenance of the underlying software platforms. Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Pharmacovigilance, and Surveillance: Conduct epidemiological and Pharmacoepidemiological research, biostatistical analyses, pharmacovigilance assessments, signal detection and evaluation, public-health surveillance, and interpretation of real-world data and evidence as required by individual scientific programs. Activities may include protocol and analysis-plan support, assessment of study limitations and bias, statistical programming, results interpretation, and technical reporting. Scientific Data Standards, Quality, and Analytics: Provide scientific expertise related to data standards, controlled terminology, study-data interpretation, data quality and fitness, and reproducible analytical methods. Support scientific data preparation and validation, biostatistics, bioinformatics, computational science, and other specialized analyses when the primary deliverable is scientific or regulatory in nature. Distinguish these activities from enterprise database administration, application development, platform engineering, and IT operations. title: 136 Airlift Wing C-130J Aircraft Wash
description: The purpose of this sources sought notice is to gain knowledge of potential sources, locations, and methods. This notice is for planning purposes only. The 136th Airlift Wing, Naval Air Station Joint Reserve Base, Fort Worth, Texas, intends to issue a solicitation and award of a contract or agreement to periodically wash C-130J model aircraft. All aircraft washing and cleaning procedures shall be performed in accordance with applicable Air Force Technical Orders, including TO 1C-130J-23CL-1 and TO 1C-130J-23S-3. Contractors shall be responsible for complying with all requirements contained within the applicable Technical Orders. Aircraft washes are to take place at an alternate location or utilize a method that allows for outdoor wash at NASJRB Fort Worth that includes collection of run-off in accordance with installation host Navy and environmental regulations. All interested parties shall submit a written response to this office, not to exceed three (3) pages, addressing the following information: Company name. Unique Entity ID (UEI) and/or CAGE Code. Location where washes would occur. A description of access requirements for the wash location. A description of prior experience with washing large aircraft, highlighting any military-type washes. Method for completing washes. Indoor or outdoor washes. Time required on location to complete washes. Availability to schedule washes at the convenience of the Government. Confirmation that all aircraft washing and cleaning procedures will be performed in accordance with TO 1C-130J-23CL-1 and TO 1C-130J-23S-3 Confirmation that only approved materials meeting MIL-PRF-87937 and MIL-PRF-85570 specifications will be used. NOTICE: Technical Orders 1C-130J-23CL-1 and 1C-130J-23S-3 contain distribution-restricted technical data and will not be provided as part of this Sources Sought Notice. Interested parties are not required to review these TOs for the purpose of responding to this notice. The requirements below identify the anticipated scope of work and key performance considerations applicable to C-130J aircraft exterior washing and corrosion control services. Any future contract award or agreement may require compliance with the current versions of applicable Technical Orders and Air Force guidance. Applicable Requirements for C-130J Aircraft Washes The contractor shall possess the capability to: Perform exterior aircraft washing of C-130J aircraft using approved aircraft cleaning methods, equipment, and materials suitable for military aircraft finishes and coatings. Utilize cleaning compounds, detergents, and wash procedures that are compatible with painted surfaces, transparencies, composite materials, antennas, sensors, and other aircraft components. Conduct freshwater rinsing procedures sufficient to remove contaminants, cleaning agents, salt deposits, dirt, oil, grease, hydraulic fluid residue, exhaust residue, and environmental pollutants. Prevent water intrusion into aircraft openings, vents, sensors, avionics components, pitot-static systems, and other sensitive areas during washing operations. Protect aircraft components and finishes from damage caused by improper washing techniques, excessive pressure, unauthorized chemicals, abrasive materials, or improper equipment use. Identify, document, and report visible signs of corrosion, coating deterioration, surface damage, fluid leaks, paint degradation, or other discrepancies observed during wash operations. Comply with all applicable Foreign Object Damage (FOD) prevention requirements while performing aircraft wash operations. Comply with all applicable environmental, hazardous material, hazardous waste, stormwater, and occupational safety regulations associated with aircraft washing activities. Provide trained and qualified personnel familiar with military aircraft washing, corrosion prevention, corrosion detection, and corrosion reporting practices. Furnish all labor, supervision, tools, equipment, cleaning materials, personal protective equipment, and transportation necessary to perform aircraft wash services. Maintain documentation of completed wash services and any corrosion or maintenance discrepancies identified during performance. Demonstrate the capability to perform aircraft washing services in a manner that supports corrosion prevention and preservation of aircraft structural integrity, protective coatings, and mission readiness. In the event that Small Business contractors are not available for adequate competition for this requirement, it may be advertised as unrestricted. Information shall be submitted via email to 136.AW.MSC@us.af.mil. Include the following subject line: �Sources Sought � Aircraft Washes � Your Company Name.� No facsimile responses will be accepted. Applicable links: MIL-PRF-87937- https://qpldocs.dla.mil/search/parts.aspx?qpl=2034 MIL-PRF-85570- https://qpldocs.dla.mil/search/parts.aspx?qpl=2132&param=MIL-PRF-85570E&type=262144

title: FCI MCKEAN GREASE TRAP PUMPING AND CLEANING SERVICES
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons intends to establish a contract for the provision of Grease Trap Cleaning Services. Services are to be performed on-site at FCI McKean. The Government reserves the right for security reasons to prohibit certain vendor employees from entering the facility. Due to the nature of the correctional setting, delays in performance of work may be expected. Such delays may include but are not limited to inclement weather, electrical or mechanical problems, or other security matters. When the contractor reports to the institution on a scheduled pickup but is unable to performance services due to such delays, the contractor will be paid for their time in the form of a predetermined trip fee. The unperformed pickup may be rescheduled at the BOP�s discretion or may be performed on the next regularly scheduled pickup. Charges for the trip fee should be represented as separate line item charges on each invoice. The point of contact for all information regarding this solicitation is Matthew Morris, PPS, at the address listed below and telephone number (814) 362-8900, extension 3420 and/or Alyssa Mcgrew at (814)362 8900 extension 3422. Offers are due no later than November 23, 2026 at 2:00PM EST. Completed offers must be emailed to m4morris@bop.gov and amcgrew@bop.gov or faxed to (814) 363-6815. Emails are preferred. If you do not receive a confirmation email, please call to verify. The anticipated award date is December 4, 2026.

title: Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Request for Information (RFI) will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this RFI is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the RFP. The following documents are attached to this RFI Notice: Attachment 1: NGTR RFI Performance Requirements - DRAFT Attachment 2: Program and Risk Feedback Matrix The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Industry Day: 2nd Quarter FY27 Estimated Draft RFP Release: 3rd Quarter FY 27 Estimated Final RFP Release: 4th Quarter FY 27 Estimated Award Date: 2nd Quarter FY 28 Target Fleet Delivery: Mid-2034 � Production-ready NGTR systems delivered to fleet locations for aircraft installation Primary Place of Performance: Contractor facility and as needed at government test sites and government facilities for meetings with NAVAIR and NSA. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. Have experience in developing and producing UHF and VHF RF radios supporting military and non-military communications waveforms. Has experience in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Have expertise and experience in reducing total life cycle support costs and utilizing predictive maintenance strategies to streamline repair procedures and reduce maintenance downtime. Have experience establishing, maintaining, and documenting a proactive DMSMS (Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages) and obsolescence programs. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing), with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,250 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5821, (Radio and Television Communication Equipment, Airborne). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. Note: FAR 52.219-14 Limitation on Subcontracting requires a small business prime on a Set-Aside to perform at least 50% of the cost of contract performance. Small business primes may now count �first tier subcontracted� work performed by similarly situated entities as if it were performed by the prime itself. To assist in market research and determination of any applicable small business set-aside for this effort, small businesses interested in priming this effort and planning to use �similarly situated entities� to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting, are requested to identify: The name & CAGE Code of the specific firm(s) intending to partner/subcontract Their small business size status under the NAICS that as the prime, you would assign for their workshare. 6.0 SUBMISSION DETAILS To ensure a fair, orderly, and efficient evaluation process, all interested parties must adhere to the following submission guidelines: 6.1 Logistics and Deadlines Response Date: All submissions must be received no later than 2:00 PM EST on 23 November 2026. Questions Deadline: Clarifying questions regarding this RFI must be submitted via email no later than 10 business days prior to the response date. 6.2 Submission Method and Point of Contact (POC) Delivery: Submissions must be sent via Electronic-mail (Email) to the Contract Specialist, Sham Keswani, at sham.v.keswani.civ@us.navy.mil. Subject Line Format: The email subject line must read: NGTR RFI Response - [Company Name]. Inquiries: No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist listed above. 6.3 Format and Structure Instructions Page Limit: Submissions must not exceed ten (10) pages total (excluding the Program and Risk Feedback Matrix in Section 7.0). Page Size & Margins: Standard 8.5 x 11-inch pages with 1-inch margins. Font: Times New Roman, font size of not less than 10 point. Document Type: Adobe PDF format. Classification: No classified information shall be submitted in response to this RFI. 6.4 Required Content Your submission package must include the following structured sections: Cover Page / Company Profile: Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, DUNS/UEI, Business Size Status under NAICS 334220, and designated Points of Contact (POC) including names, phone numbers, and email addresses. Capabilities Statement: A detailed narrative addressing your ability to meet the special requirements and required capabilities outlined in Section 4.0. Program and Risk Feedback: Completed responses to the targeted questions and the structured feedback matrix outlined in Section 7.0. 6.5 Proprietary Data and Information Handling All data received in response to this RFI that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government. Any information or materials provided in response to this RFI Notice will not be returned. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise resulting from responses to this RF

The IDIQ contract would also include the sampling and testing of dredged material proposed for upland placement. �Upland� sampling and testing would adhere to the procedures, and their subsequent updates, as described in: New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection (NJDEP) New Jersey Administrative Code (NJAC), Title 7, Chapters 9 and 26 (a.k.a. �NJAC 7�) (https://dep.nj.gov/rules/current-rules-and-regulations/) New York State Department of Environmental Conservation (NYSDEC) manual, entitled �Technical & Operational Guidance Series (TOGS) 5.1.9 In-Water and Riparian Management of Sediment and Dredged Material� (November 2004) (a.k.a. �TOGS 5.1.9�) (https://www.dec.ny.gov/docs/water_pdf/togs519.pdf) New York State Department of Environmental Conservation, New York Codes, Rules and Regulations (NYCRR), Title 6, Part 375 (December 2025) (a.k.a. �6 NYCRR Part 375�) (https://dec.ny.gov/sites/default/files/2025-12/6nycrrpart375final.pdf). Other state procedures may also be requested and would be coordinated between NYD and the contractor to determine capabilities. Additional work under this contract will include analyses of sediment, tissue, and water and may include environmental DNA/metagenomic analyses related to HARS monitoring in accordance with the following document and any subsequent updates: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) New York District and Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Region 2, Site Management and Monitoring Plan for Historic Area Remediation Site (HARS) (July 2020). Task orders would include all or some of the following: sediment and water collection (on Contractor-supplied ship) handling, processing and shipping of samples physical and chemical analyses quality assurance (QA) and quality control (QC) procedures, and necessary corrective actions. For each task order, the contractor would provide reports containing the sampling logs, all testing results and QA/QC information in the format required by NYD, EPA � Region 2, and/or state agencies. In addition to sampling and testing for ocean placement, NYD also requires that contractors be capable of performing testing procedures such as the Synthetic Precipitation Leaching Procedure (SPLP), the Toxicity Characteristic Leaching Procedure (TCLP), and the Modified Elutriate Test (MET), which are required for upland placement of dredged material in the states of New York and New Jersey. Prior to sampling and testing, a Work/Quality Assurance (QA) Plan and an Accident Prevention Plan (APP) would need to be prepared by the contractor and approved by NYD. A Work/QA Plan must include: descriptions of all technical procedures for field sampling, laboratory analyses (e.g. biological, physical) for HARS and upland testing, data reduction and validation, and reporting clearly written standard operating procedures (SOP) for all field, experimental and analytical procedures clearly defined QA objectives that are consistent with the regulations (e.g. Regional Testing Manual, Green Book, NJAC 7, TOGS 5.1.9, and 6 NYCRR Part 375) and if applicable, permit application mechanisms for conducting performance and systems audits during the course of the field laboratory work procedures for detecting problems with sampling and analytical work, and implementation of corrective actions in a timely manner. All sampling would be performed within the Port of New York & New Jersey, all Federal Navigation Channels within New York District, the length of the Hudson River, in the Atlantic Ocean at the Historic Area Remediation Site and its Mud Dump Reference Site. �New Work or Harbor Deepening� projects may be proposed and coordinated between NYD and the contractor. A detailed description of work required for these contracts will be provided in its entirety upon issuance of the complete solicitation. Prior to issuance of the solicitation, it is highly recommended that interested parties read the required regulations (e.g. Regional Testing Manual, Green Book, NJAC 7, TOGS 5.1.9, and 6 NYCRR Part 375) in order to obtain a thorough understanding of the work required by the NYD and EPA � Region 2 dredged material testing program. The Period of Performance will be five (5) years from the issuance of the Notice to Proceed (NTP). The contract magnitude will be up to $10,000,000.00 for five (5) years � up to $2,000,000.00 each year. One contract will be awarded on an Unrestricted Full and Open Competition basis to the lowest bidder who has, within the last 18 months, demonstrated their capability of performing the program�s work to EPA � Region 2. A bidder can prove their capability through one of the following: the bidder has received, within the last 18 months from EPA � Region 2, documentation stating that the laboratory has submitted data that is fully acceptable or acceptable with qualification; or the bidder has satisfied the Demonstration of Capability (DOC) requirements for the NYD and EPA � Region 2 dredged material testing program. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541380. The business size standard is $25,500,000.

title: Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR)
description: 1.0 INTRODUCTION The Naval Air Systems Command (NAVAIR), PMA-209, located at Naval Air Station Patuxent River, Maryland, is seeking information from potential sources regarding a modular Software Defined Radio (SDR) for U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft, designated the Next Generation Tactical Radio (NGTR). The NGTR is intended to support voice and data waveforms in the Very High Frequency (VHF) and Ultra High Frequency (UHF) bands, with operational capability extending up to 6 GHz. It will incorporate a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) to meet National Security Agency (NSA) cryptographic and Security Evaluation Requirements Document (SERD) requirements. Additionally, the NGTR is designed to serve as a form, fit, and function backwards-compatible replacement for aircraft currently equipped with the ARC-210 Generation 5 and Generation 6 radios. This Market Research tool is being used to identify potential and eligible firms, of all sizes, prior to determining the method of acquisition and issuance of a solicitation. The results of the Request for Information (RFI) will be utilized to determine if any Small Business Set-Aside opportunities exist. Additionally, this RFI is being used to gather constructive information from industry to improve the RFP. The following documents are attached to this RFI Notice: Attachment 1: NGTR RFI Performance Requirements - DRAFT Attachment 2: Program and Risk Feedback Matrix The following dates are anticipated time frames associated with this requirement: Estimated Industry Day: 1st Quarter FY27 Estimated Draft RFP Release: 3rd Quarter FY 27 Estimated Final RFP Release: 4th Quarter FY 27 Estimated Award Date: 2nd Quarter FY 28 Target Fleet Delivery: Mid-2034 � Production-ready NGTR systems delivered to fleet locations for aircraft installation Primary Place of Performance: Contractor facility and as needed at government test sites and government facilities for meetings with NAVAIR and NSA. 2.0 DISCLAIMER THIS REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL. IT DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS REQUEST IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. 3.0 PROGRAM BACKGROUND The NGTR system's goal is to develop a small form factor system compatible with existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft that will support: Communications waveforms in the VHF, UHF frequency bands with support for waveforms up to 6GHz. Waveforms defined in Attachment 1. A Modular, Open architecture to support rapid capability integration and obsolescence upgrades including a modular High Assurance Device (HAD) that supports NSA cryptographic and SERD requirements. Zero Trust System security meeting applicable Risk Management Framework (RMF) controls. Minimal integration impact and modification requirements for existing and future U.S. Navy and Marine Corps aircraft platforms. 4.0 SPECIAL REQUIREMENTS AND REQUIRED CAPABILITIES The NGTR system is expected to meet the performance requirements defined in Attachment 1: �NGTR RFI Performance Requirements� - DRAFT. The NGTR Contractor is expected to meet the following qualifications: Have secure military software defined radios with embedded NSA certified cryptography. Have experience in agile and modular development and testing, incorporating customer feedback throughout the process. Have the ability to obtain Top Secret security clearances for employees and facility within 12 months of contract award, including the ability to support development and test up to the Top Secret level. Have experience in developing and producing UHF and VHF RF radios supporting military and non-military communications waveforms. Has experience in Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE). Have expertise and experience in reducing total life cycle support costs and utilizing predictive maintenance strategies to streamline repair procedures and reduce maintenance downtime. Have experience establishing, maintaining, and documenting a proactive DMSMS (Diminishing Manufacturing Sources and Material Shortages) and obsolescence programs. 5.0 ELIGIBILITY The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this requirement is 334220 (Radio and Television Broadcasting and Wireless Communications Equipment Manufacturing), with a Small Business Size Standard of 1,250 Employees. The Product Service Code (PSC) is 5821, (Radio and Television Communication Equipment, Airborne). Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond; however, each respondent must clearly identify their business size in their capabilities statement. Note: FAR 52.219-14 Limitation on Subcontracting requires a small business prime on a Set-Aside to perform at least 50% of the cost of contract performance. Small business primes may now count �first tier subcontracted� work performed by similarly situated entities as if it were performed by the prime itself. To assist in market research and determination of any applicable small business set-aside for this effort, small businesses interested in priming this effort and planning to use �similarly situated entities� to meet the Limitations on Subcontracting, are requested to identify: The name & CAGE Code of the specific firm(s) intending to partner/subcontract Their small business size status under the NAICS that as the prime, you would assign for their workshare. 6.0 SUBMISSION DETAILS To ensure a fair, orderly, and efficient evaluation process, all interested parties must adhere to the following submission guidelines: 6.1 Logistics and Deadlines Response Date: All submissions must be received no later than 2:00 PM EST on 23 November 2026. Questions Deadline: Clarifying questions regarding this RFI must be submitted via email no later than 10 business days prior to the response date. 6.2 Submission Method and Point of Contact (POC) Delivery: Submissions must be sent via Electronic-mail (Email) to the Contract Specialist, Sham Keswani, at sham.v.keswani.civ@us.navy.mil. Subject Line Format: The email subject line must read: NGTR RFI Response - [Company Name]. Inquiries: No phone calls will be accepted. All questions must be submitted via email to the Contract Specialist listed above. 6.3 Format and Structure Instructions Page Limit: Submissions must not exceed ten (10) pages total (excluding the Program and Risk Feedback Matrix in Section 7.0). Page Size & Margins: Standard 8.5 x 11-inch pages with 1-inch margins. Font: Times New Roman, font size of not less than 10 point. Document Type: Adobe PDF format. Classification: No classified information shall be submitted in response to this RFI. 6.4 Required Content Your submission package must include the following structured sections: Cover Page / Company Profile: Company Name, Address, CAGE Code, DUNS/UEI, Business Size Status under NAICS 334220, and designated Points of Contact (POC) including names, phone numbers, and email addresses. Capabilities Statement: A detailed narrative addressing your ability to meet the special requirements and required capabilities outlined in Section 4.0. Program and Risk Feedback: Completed responses to the targeted questions and the structured feedback matrix outlined in Section 7.0. 6.5 Proprietary Data and Information Handling All data received in response to this RFI that is marked or designated as corporate or proprietary will be fully protected from any release outside the Government. Any information or materials provided in response to this RFI Notice will not be returned. The Government is not committed nor obligated to pay for the information provided, and no basis for claims against the Government shall arise resulting from responses to this RF

title: FCI MCKEAN GREASE TRAP PUMPING AND CLEANING SERVICES
description: **AMMENDMENT 1. REMOVED INCORRECT WAGE DETERMINATION AND UPLOADED CORRECT WAGE DETERMINATION*** **AMMENDMENT 2. UPLOADED AMENDMENT DOCUMENT 15B20927Q00000001 P00001 RFQ GREASE TRAP.pdf THIS DOCUMENT UPDATES THE OPTION YEARS IN LINE ITEMS 2 THROUGH 5. TO BEGIN ON OCTOBER 1 INSTEAD OF DECEMBER. UPDATED TERMS AND CONDITIONS. ADDED 52.217-9 AND REMOVED 52.226-3. **** The Federal Bureau of Prisons intends to establish a contract for the provision of Grease Trap Cleaning Services. Services are to be performed on-site at FCI McKean. Place of Performance Place of Performance will be located at FCI McKean, 6975 Route 59 Lewis Run, PA 16738. Schedule The contractor will provide grease trap cleaning and waste disposal at the scheduled times below. The specific days for performance of these services will be established after contract award. The contractor will be required to provide these services on an estimated two to three month interval between the hours of 7:30AM-3:00PM, Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays. The exact intervals between cleanings will be determined as needed by the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR). FCI McKean has one 10,000 gallon trap within the secure confines behind the Food Service department, and one 2,000 gallon trap at the satellite prison camp. All grease and pumpings removed shall be disposed of in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations. The contractor shall furnish an invoice for each service delivered at the time of extraction. All extractions and cleanings will be verified and signed for by an authorized representative. Specific Requirements The contractor will be licensed/permitted by the State of Pennsylvania and will provide evidence of proper waste disposal, in accordance with all current Federal, State, and local codes, laws, and requirements regarding the disposal of solid waste. Supplies and Equipment The contractor will provide the truck, labor, and equipment necessary for effective removal, transportation/disposal of waste. All material located within the container upon removal become the property and responsibility of the contractor to dispose of in a lawful manner. Description of Duties The contractor has sole responsibility and discretion for choosing and implementing the manner and method of performing tasks outlined in the Statement of Work as long as the requirements are met in accordance with the policies described above. The services, although not directly supervised, shall be reviewed by institution staff to ensure contract compliance. Contractor performance will be monitored by the COR and evaluated in accordance with FAR Part 42. Institution Security The contractor agrees to adhere to all regulations prescribed by the institution for the safety, custody, and conduct of inmates. Access to the containers will be available only during the scheduled hours, unless prior approval of the COR is obtained. All contract personnel that are entering the secure confines of the institution are required to have a clear NCIC background check.While on institution grounds and prior to departure, the operator, equipment, and vehicle shall be subject to security checks and inspections. The Government reserves the right for security reasons to prohibit certain vendor employees from entering the facility. Due to the nature of the correctional setting, delays in performance of work may be expected. Such delays may include but are not limited to inclement weather, electrical or mechanical problems, or other security matters. When the contractor reports to the institution on a scheduled pickup but is unable to performance services due to such delays, the contractor will be paid for their time in the form of a predetermined trip fee. The unperformed pickup may be rescheduled at the BOP�s discretion or may be performed on the next regularly scheduled pickup. Charges for the trip fee should be represented as separate line item charges on each invoice. The point of contact for all information regarding this solicitation is Matthew Morris, PPS, at the address listed below and telephone number (814) 362-8900, extension 3420 and/or Alyssa Mcgrew at (814)362 8900 extension 3422. Offers are due no later than November 23, 2026 at 2:00PM EST. Completed offers must be emailed to m4morris@bop.gov and amcgrew@bop.gov or faxed to (814) 363-6815. Emails are preferred. If you do not receive a confirmation email, please call to verify. The anticipated award date is December 4, 2026.

description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY. This is not a solicitation or a request for proposal and no contract will be awarded from this notice. Work also includes integrated mission-specific systems such as reliable power, 24/7 HVAC, communications/IT infrastructure, security systems, laboratory support, resilient infrastructure, and an emergency generator. NAICS Code: Construction of Buildings - 236220 - Commercial and Institutional Building Construction with a size standard of $45 Million. Company profile, to include number of employees, annual receipts, office location(s), and SAM UEI. Evidence to establish your company's standing as a SDVOSB, HUBZone, EDWOSB or 8(a) small business concern, under applicable NAICS. A positive statement of your intention to submit a bid for this requirement if set-aside for your socio-economic group. AGAIN, THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. Responses must be received no later than 2:00 PM, Local Time on November 23, 2026. Please submit your capability statement via e-mail to Molly A. Lewis, Contract Officer, at Molly.Lewis@gsa.gov. Questions regarding this notice may be addressed to Molly.Lewis@gsa.gov. Failure to submit all information requested will result in a contractor not being considered as an interested small business concern.

title: Sources Sought Mitchell Hall Uniforms
description: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE IS FOR MARKET RESEARCH AND PLANNING PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTATION, REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL, OR SOLICITATION. RESPONSES WILL NOT BE TREATED AS OFFERS, AND THE GOVERNMENT WILL NOT MAKE AN AWARD OR PAY FOR INFORMATION PROVIDED IN RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE. The United States Air Force Academy, 10th Contracting Squadron, is conducting market research to identify capable commercial and small-business sources for Mitchell Hall employee uniforms, embroidery, screen printing, delivery, and related support. The Government is evaluating whether to establish one or more Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) to support recurring, as-needed purchases of commercial uniform items and related services for Mitchell Hall personnel. Any future BPA would not guarantee a minimum quantity, dollar value, ordering frequency, or purchase volume. The Government would be obligated only to the extent of authorized purchases actually made under any future BPA. Mitchell Hall currently supports approximately 110 uniformed personnel and anticipates an average of approximately five new hires per month. These figures are planning estimates only. The attached draft uniform item list identifies the Government�s current anticipated items, colors, size ranges, customization requirements, and manufacturer/style references. The attached embroidery artwork identifies current logo embroidery and placement requirements. Manufacturer and style references are provided for market-research purposes only. The Government has not yet determined whether the final solicitation will require exact manufacturer/style items or permit comparable commercial items that meet the Government�s needs. Certain legacy items may no longer be commercially available. Respondents should identify any item that cannot be furnished as listed and may propose a commercially available alternative for Government consideration. Interested parties are requested to provide the information below. 1. Capability Confirm whether your company can provide: Uniform items identified in the draft item list; AF United States Air Force Academy and Mitchell Hall USAFA logo embroidery; Name embroidery and screen printing, as required; Government Purchase Card payment; Standard delivery within 30 calendar days after receipt of an order; and Prepaid return labels, when required, for incorrect, damaged, defective, or otherwise nonconforming items. 2. Item Availability and Proposed Alternatives For each item your company cannot furnish as listed, provide: Affected item description; Proposed alternate manufacturer and style number; Color and available size range; Product literature, catalog page, or website link; Material differences from the listed item, including fabric, fit, pockets, construction, or appearance; and Estimated delivery lead time. Respondents should identify whether proposed alternatives are commercially available and available for recurring purchase. 3. Nonbinding Commercial Pricing Information Respondents are requested to provide current commercial catalog pricing, price-list information, or representative pricing ranges for the following categories: Chef coats and chef pants; Work shirts, polos, and T-shirts; Work/cargo pants; Hats, caps, and aprons; Logo embroidery; Name embroidery; Screen printing; Digitizing/setup charges, if applicable; Shipping charges, if applicable; and Available quantity discounts. Respondents are not required to submit a completed pricing template or binding quotation. Any pricing information submitted is for market-research purposes only. 4. Vendor Administration and Order Support Provide: Legal business name; UEI and CAGE, if available; Small-business status and any applicable socioeconomic status; Whether the company is a manufacturer, dealer, reseller, distributor, or other supplier; Primary and alternate points of contact; Ordering email address and telephone number; Confirmation that the company can acknowledge Government order requests within one business day; Confirmation that the company can provide an availability, lead-time, or substitution response within two business days; Confirmation that the company can submit updated price lists annually for Contracting Officer review and approval; and Confirmation that substitutions would not be provided without Government approval. 5.
