description: This is not a solicitation announcement. This is a Sources Sought Notice (SSN) only. This SSN is issued solely for market research and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFP in the future. Further, the SSN does not commit the Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. The FDA is not seeking proposals and will not accept any unsolicited proposals. Responders are advised that the U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this SSN; all costs associated with responding to this SSN will be solely at the expense of the interested respondents. Not responding to this SSN does not preclude participation in any future RFP, if issued. The purpose of this sources sought synopsis is to gain knowledge of potential qualified vendors to include potential 8(a) vendors 8(a) relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code and capable of providing multidisciplinary scientific and regulatory professional services in support of FDA Centers and Offices. Responses to this Sources Sought Notice will be used by the Government to make appropriate determinations about potential sources. Project Title: FDA Scientific and Regulatory Support Services (SRS) IDIQ Background/Overview: The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is a science-based regulatory agency critically important to the stability of the nation's public health and health care systems. FDA protects and promotes the health and safety of all Americans by enhancing the availability of safe medical products, foods, and animal products, and by promoting innovation that addresses unmet medical and public health needs. FDA decisions must be based on the best available scientific data and employ the best tools and methods available to ensure products meet the highest quality standards, while fostering innovation in the products it regulates. In support of its regulatory mission, FDA conducts scientific research across a broad range of disciplines including vaccines, drug safety, food safety, medical devices, biologics, toxicology, radiological products, and more. FDA's science is increasingly data-centric, complex, and collaborative, involving multidisciplinary groups across its Centers and Offices. Within the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research (CDER), the Office of Computational Science (OCS), established under the Office of Translational Sciences, supports the data management, technical, and analytic needs of the regulatory review process. OCS manages and supports analytical tools, data standards, and computing infrastructure that form the backbone of modern regulatory review for medical products. Purpose: The FDA is seeking information from experienced sources in Scientific and Regulatory Support Services as it is contemplating the establishment of a Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) to such services. The FDA�s primary objective for this effect is to obtain Contractor services related to scientific and regulatory support across a broad range of mission requirements. Depending on the requirement, services may support scientific research, regulatory review, clinical and non-clinical analyses, epidemiology and surveillance, scientific data interpretation, laboratory activities, technical writing, training, and scientific program coordination. Objectives: The objective of the contemplated SRS acquisition is to provide FDA with responsive, high-quality scientific and regulatory support across a broad range of mission requirements. Depending on the task order, services may support scientific research, regulatory review, clinical and nonclinical analyses, epidemiology and surveillance, scientific data interpretation, laboratory activities, technical writing, training, and scientific program coordination. The Government is interested in sources capable of providing the scientific depth and operational capacity needed to: Conduct scientifically sound analyses and prepare defensible, traceable technical products supporting FDA review and public-health decisions. Provide qualified personnel across multiple scientific and regulatory disciplines, including specialized and emerging areas. Support clinical and nonclinical study-data review, standardized scientific datasets, statistical computing, data fitness, quality assessment, and interpretation. Respond to multiple simultaneous task orders, changing priorities, time-sensitive scientific questions, and evolving requirements across FDA organizations. Maintain scientific quality, data integrity, documentation, confidentiality, and continuity of performance. Deliver effective scientific training, technical writing, knowledge transfer, and program-management support tied directly to scientific and regulatory missions. Project Requirements: The following descriptions are illustrative of the types of services that may be ordered. They are provided to inform industry responses and do not establish final task-order requirements. Each task order would define its own objectives, tasks, deliverables, performance expectations, staffing qualifications, and period of performance. Scientific Research and Regulatory Review Support: Support scientific investigations, literature and evidence reviews, research planning, study design, methodological assessments, scientific consultations, and technical analyses relevant to FDA-regulated products. Prepare scientific assessments, briefing materials, review support documentation, and other products that allow Government scientists and reviewers to evaluate scientific evidence and communicate findings. Provide subject-matter expertise to address complex or emerging regulatory science questions. Clinical and Nonclinical Study-Data Review and Analysis: Support the scientific review of clinical and nonclinical datasets submitted for regulatory purposes, including data fitness and completeness assessments, exploratory safety analyses, descriptive and inferential statistical analyses, and preparation of tables, listings, figures, and visualizations. Experience with standards such as CDISC SDTM, ADaM, and SEND may be relevant. The RRS BPA describes review-oriented services that assess study data and produce analyses for FDA reviewers; SRS would focus on the scientific and analytical performance of those services rather than maintenance of the underlying software platforms. Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Pharmacovigilance, and Surveillance: Conduct epidemiological and Pharmacoepidemiological research, biostatistical analyses, pharmacovigilance assessments, signal detection and evaluation, public-health surveillance, and interpretation of real-world data and evidence as required by individual scientific programs. Activities may include protocol and analysis-plan support, assessment of study limitations and bias, statistical programming, results interpretation, and technical reporting. Scientific Data Standards, Quality, and Analytics: Provide scientific expertise related to data standards, controlled terminology, study-data interpretation, data quality and fitness, and reproducible analytical methods. Support scientific data preparation and validation, biostatistics, bioinformatics, computational science, and other specialized analyses when the primary deliverable is scientific or regulatory in nature. Distinguish these activities from enterprise database administration, application development, platform engineering, and IT operations. Laboratory and Specialized Scientific Support: Provide laboratory-related scientific and technical expertise, research assistance, analytical method support, study coordination, quality documentation, and interpretation or reporting of laboratory findings where required by a task order. title: 136 Airlift Wing C-130J Aircraft Wash
description: The purpose of this sources sought notice is to gain knowledge of potential sources, locations, and methods. This notice is for planning purposes only. The 136th Airlift Wing, Naval Air Station Joint Reserve Base, Fort Worth, Texas, intends to issue a solicitation and award of a contract or agreement to periodically wash C-130J model aircraft. All aircraft washing and cleaning procedures shall be performed in accordance with applicable Air Force Technical Orders, including TO 1C-130J-23CL-1 and TO 1C-130J-23S-3. Contractors shall be responsible for complying with all requirements contained within the applicable Technical Orders. Aircraft washes are to take place at an alternate location or utilize a method that allows for outdoor wash at NASJRB Fort Worth that includes collection of run-off in accordance with installation host Navy and environmental regulations. All interested parties shall submit a written response to this office, not to exceed three (3) pages, addressing the following information: Company name. Unique Entity ID (UEI) and/or CAGE Code. Location where washes would occur. A description of access requirements for the wash location. A description of prior experience with washing large aircraft, highlighting any military-type washes. Method for completing washes. Indoor or outdoor washes. Time required on location to complete washes. Availability to schedule washes at the convenience of the Government. Confirmation that all aircraft washing and cleaning procedures will be performed in accordance with TO 1C-130J-23CL-1 and TO 1C-130J-23S-3 Confirmation that only approved materials meeting MIL-PRF-87937 and MIL-PRF-85570 specifications will be used. NOTICE: Technical Orders 1C-130J-23CL-1 and 1C-130J-23S-3 contain distribution-restricted technical data and will not be provided as part of this Sources Sought Notice. Interested parties are not required to review these TOs for the purpose of responding to this notice. The requirements below identify the anticipated scope of work and key performance considerations applicable to C-130J aircraft exterior washing and corrosion control services. Any future contract award or agreement may require compliance with the current versions of applicable Technical Orders and Air Force guidance. Applicable Requirements for C-130J Aircraft Washes The contractor shall possess the capability to: Perform exterior aircraft washing of C-130J aircraft using approved aircraft cleaning methods, equipment, and materials suitable for military aircraft finishes and coatings. Utilize cleaning compounds, detergents, and wash procedures that are compatible with painted surfaces, transparencies, composite materials, antennas, sensors, and other aircraft components. Conduct freshwater rinsing procedures sufficient to remove contaminants, cleaning agents, salt deposits, dirt, oil, grease, hydraulic fluid residue, exhaust residue, and environmental pollutants. Prevent water intrusion into aircraft openings, vents, sensors, avionics components, pitot-static systems, and other sensitive areas during washing operations. Protect aircraft components and finishes from damage caused by improper washing techniques, excessive pressure, unauthorized chemicals, abrasive materials, or improper equipment use. Identify, document, and report visible signs of corrosion, coating deterioration, surface damage, fluid leaks, paint degradation, or other discrepancies observed during wash operations. Comply with all applicable Foreign Object Damage (FOD) prevention requirements while performing aircraft wash operations. Comply with all applicable environmental, hazardous material, hazardous waste, stormwater, and occupational safety regulations associated with aircraft washing activities. Provide trained and qualified personnel familiar with military aircraft washing, corrosion prevention, corrosion detection, and corrosion reporting practices. Furnish all labor, supervision, tools, equipment, cleaning materials, personal protective equipment, and transportation necessary to perform aircraft wash services. Maintain documentation of completed wash services and any corrosion or maintenance discrepancies identified during performance. Demonstrate the capability to perform aircraft washing services in a manner that supports corrosion prevention and preservation of aircraft structural integrity, protective coatings, and mission readiness. In the event that Small Business contractors are not available for adequate competition for this requirement, it may be advertised as unrestricted. Information shall be submitted via email to 136.AW.MSC@us.af.mil. Include the following subject line: �Sources Sought � Aircraft Washes � Your Company Name.� No facsimile responses will be accepted. Applicable links: MIL-PRF-87937- https://qpldocs.dla.mil/search/parts.aspx?qpl=2034 MIL-PRF-85570- https://qpldocs.dla.mil/search/parts.aspx?qpl=2132&param=MIL-PRF-85570E&type=262144

title: Unaccompanied Personnel Housing Restoration at NSB Kings Bay, GA
description: THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT, A MARKET SURVEY FOR WRITTEN INFORMATION ONLY TO IDENTIFY POTENTIAL OFFERORS FOR A DESIGN-BID-BUILD CONSTRUCTION PROJECT TO RENOVATE THE UNACCOMPANIED ENLISTED PERSONNEL HOUSING QUARTERS (BUILDINGS 1042, 1044, 1045, 1046 AND 1054) LOCATED AT NAVAL SUBMARINE BASE (SUBBASE) KINGS BAY, GA. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS OR AN INVITATION FOR BID. NO CONTRACT WILL BE AWARDED FROM THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. NO REIMBURSEMENT WILL BE MADE FOR ANY COSTS ASSOCIATED WITH PROVIDING INFORMATION IN RESPONSE TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT OR ANY FOLLOW-UP INFORMATION REQUESTS. No telephone calls will be accepted requesting a bid package or solicitation. There is no bid package or solicitation currently available. In order to protect the procurement integrity of any future procurement that may arise from this announcement, information regarding the technical point of contact will not be given and no appointments for presentations will be made. The reference number for this posting is N6945027RUPHR. The purpose of this notice is for the Naval Facilities Engineering Systems Command Southeast (NAVFAC SE) to gain knowledge of ALL qualified and interested parties. All socioeconomic categories are encouraged to respond: U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) certified 8(a), SBA certified HUBZone, woman-owned small business (WOSB), veteran-owned small business (VOSB), and service disabled veteran-owned small business (SDVOSB). Potential sources should have current relevant qualifications, experience, personnel, and capability to perform this proposed project. The Government may use the sources sought responses along with other market research to make various determinations regarding the procurement. Project Description: This project will include, but is not limited to, renovate the Unaccompanied Enlisted Personnel Housing Quarters (Buildings 1042, 1044, 1045, 1046 and 1054) located at Naval Submarine Base (SUBBASE), Kings Bay, Georgia. Buildings 1042, 1044, 1045 and 1046 were constructed in 1984. Building 1054 was constructed in 1989. The project scope includes upgrades to mechanical systems, fire protection, fire alarms, bathrooms, and exterior renovation. Except for Air Handling Units (AHU) in Buildings 1042, 1044 and 1046, all mechanical systems are being upgraded under this project. Mechanical system repairs include replacement of HVAC AHUs, installing Direct Digital Controls (DDC) for temperature and humidity, replacement of chilled water (CHW) piping, circulation pumps and cleaning of ductwork. Plumbing repairs include the replacement of plumbing fixtures, domestic water piping and sanitary piping. Electrical system repairs include replacement of electrical service panels throughout the building. Electrical repairs also include replacement of lighting fixtures with LED fixtures and replacement of wiring and wiring devices where they do not meet the current codes. Exterior renovation includes replacement of gutters, windows, doors, safety railings, lights. Interior renovation includes remodeling of bathrooms, mold remediation, and cleaning and painting of all previously painted surfaces. Ceilings and non-loadbearing walls will be demolished and rebuilt as required to allow access to rebuild mechanical and plumbing ductwork and pipes. The project also requires the design for abatement of hazardous material. The hazardous materials survey has been conducted by the industrial hygiene professionals, and the findings of the survey are included in the report. The anticipated performance period for this contract will be 1200 calendar days. The magnitude of construction is between $25,000,000 and $50,000,000. The anticipated award date is fourth Quarter FY 27. Interested sources are invited to respond to this Sources Sought announcement. Capability Statements consisting of appropriate documentation will be accepted providing it contains ALL the information required below (items 1-7). Complete submission package shall not exceed 6 pages. The information which must be contained in your response is as follows: 1) Contractor Information: Name and address of company, point of contact with phone number and email address. 2) Type of Business: Identify the company�s business size and socio-economic status (HUBZone, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.) if applicable for NAICS Code 236200 applicable to this sources sought. If your firm is claiming HUBZone or 8(a) status, provide a copy of your SBA certification. 3) Bond Capacity: Information must include surety�s name, point of contact, telephone number, email address, and the bonding capacity of at least $50 Million per project, and the maximum aggregate bonding. 4) System for Award Management (SAM): Evidence of registration in the SAM, including Cage Code and Unique Entity Identifier. 5) Interest: Indicate if a solicitation is issued will your firm/company be submitting a proposal: _____ Yes ______No. 6) Existing Contract Vehicles your firm may have (GWAC, FSS, MACC, MATOC, etc.) available for this work. 7) Experience Submission Requirements: Responders shall provide a minimum of three (3) to a maximum of five (5) projects demonstrating Prime construction experience demonstrating the specific capabilities listed below: Executing construction or major renovations of multi-story, multi-unit living quarters facilities including dormitories, multi-family housing, hotels, office buildings or other similar types of construction. Projects submitted for the Offeror shall be valued at $20 million or greater and/or 30,000 square feet or greater. Completed within the past seven (7) years of the date of issuance of this announcement. Provide a brief description including contract number, project title, completion date, performance ratings, and final contract value. If they are not approximately equal to the requested dollar value, identify the dollar value and explain in no more than one paragraph why we should consider the project. The response to this sources sought is not expected to be a proposal, but rather short statements regarding the company�s ability to demonstrate experience in relation to the areas specified herein. Submission of Capabilities statement is not a prerequisite to any potential future offerings, but participation will assist the Government in tailoring requirements to be consistent with industry capabilities. Please respond to this announcement no later than 23 NOV 2026, 2:00 PM Eastern Time via email to Darrien Thomas at darrien.a.thomas.civ@us.navy.mil and Aimee Johnson at aimee.n.johnson2.civ@us.navy.mil. The subject line of the email shall state: Unaccompanied Personnel Housing Restoration, NSB Kings Bay. Emails shall be no more than 5 MB in size. Responses that do not meet all requirements or are not submitted within the allotted time will not be considered. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation.

description: 18 November 2026 UPDATE: Virtual Industry Day was held on Monday, 16 November 2026. The Presentation, Attendence List, and Questions & Answers are now uploaded to this Notice. Sources sought Responses are due 23 November 2026 at 1400 pm EST to susan.k.ellis@usace.army.mil and nicholas.lizotte@usace.army.mil. ___________________________________________________________ W91236 27X1CTA Sources Sought Notice DOWEA Preventative Maintenance Demand Maintenance- Puerto Rico IDIQ at Ft. Buchanan, San Juan and Ramey Unit School, Aguadilla This is a Sources Sought Notice only; it is not a request for competitive proposals. There is no solicitation, specifications, and/or drawings available at this time. The purpose of this Sources Sought Notice is to identify business concerns with sufficient similar experience that are capable and interested in performing the work described herein. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any cost incurred in preparation of a response to this notice. The Government intends to use responses to this Sources Sought to make appropriate acquisition decisions for the project. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought notice. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Norfolk District is anticipating a new procurement for a Firm-Fixed Price Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) Services contract, for the Department of War Education Activity (DoWEA) Preventative Maintenance (PM) and Demand Maintenance (DM) at Ft. Buchanan, San Juan and Ramey Unit School, Aguadilla, Puerto Rico. Description of Work USACE, Norfolk District is seeking eligible firms capable of Preventative Maintenance and Demand Maintenance repair services in support of the DoWEA-America�s facilities located at Ft. Buchanan, San Juan and Ramey Unit School, Aguadilla, Puerto Rico. The services provided under this proposed contract encompass facilities total maintenance services such as operation and maintenance of heating, ventilation and cooling systems, kitchen equipment, facility control systems, playgrounds, plumbing, electrical, and fire alarms, building systems, roofs, and other facility systems and components. These services must be provided on an ongoing basis without protracted lapse to ensure that the building systems continue to operate efficiently and safely for the benefit of the students and teachers that inhabit them. The facilities under this action which require Preventative Maintenance & Demand Repair Maintenance include a total of five (5) buildings comprised of three (3) schools and one (1) support facility at Ft. Buchanan, San Juan for an approximate total of 320,870 GSF; and one (1) Ramey Unit School at Aguadilla for an approximate total of 122,539 GSF. Solicitation Anticipated solicitation issuance timeframe is on or about January 2027, and the estimated solicitation period of 30 calendar days with a proposal due date timeframe on or about February 2027. The project consists of a 12-month base period, four (4) option years for a total of five (5) years. NAICS Code 238220 - Plumbing, Heating, and Air-Conditioning Contractors applies with a Small Business Size Standard of $19,000,000.00 Offerors will be evaluated on a Best-Value Tradeoff basis with a combination of price and non-price factors. All interested firms shall be registered in SAM.GOV and PIEE in order to submit a proposal in response to the solicitation when issued. VIRTUAL INDUSTRY DAY NOTICE The Government will host a Virtual Industry Day to engage with interested parties and address questions related to this requirement. Participation in the Virtual Industry Day is voluntary and is not required to submit a capabilities statement. The Virtual Industry Day will be held on Monday, 16 NOV 2026 from 0900-1000 AM Eastern Standard Time (EST). A Microsoft Teams meeting invite will be provided to interested firms who RSVP by email no later than 12 NOV 2026 to Susan Ellis at susan.k.ellis@usace.army.mil and Nicholas Lizotte at nicholas.lizotte@usace.army.mil. INFORMATION REQUESTED FROM INDUSTRY All interested, capable, qualified, and responsive SMALL BUSINESS Prime Contractors are encouraged to reply to this Sources Sought announcement. Interested contractors should furnish the following information: Company name, address, phone number, and point of contact information. Indicate business size in relation to the NAICS Code 238220. Provide your company's Unique Entity Identification number (UEI) to verify your business status as a qualified Small Business (SB), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned SB (SDVOSB), Historically Underutilized Business Zones (HUBZones), Qualified Section 8(a), Women-Owned or other than Small Business. Contractors must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) at time of proposal submission and contract award. Please see www.SAM.gov for additional registration information. Provide a narrative describing primary business lines and the geographic regions your company serves. Narratives shall be no longer than five (5) pages demonstrating experience in a similar type of work as described above, at similar contract values, and in similar locations. Does your company, through in-house forces or subcontract support, have the technical capability and capacity to provide preventive maintenance and demand maintenance repair services for the facilities and locations as described above? Given the Facility Coverage requirements listed in the description of work: what level of staffing would you suggest for full-time employees to be on-site (full time) to fulfill these requirements. Please include the trades as well as the personnel�s pertinent certifications/licenses. The Government intends to include a Limit of Liability (LOL) in this contract for repairs the Contractor would be responsible for under the firm-fixed price portion of this contract. The Contractor�s limit of liability (LoL) for material and labor costs associated with any single demand maintenance event including repair or replacement of any single piece of equipment is $20,000 without limit of maintenance occurrences per year. The Government will utilize this information in determining an Acquisition Strategy. Please submit capability packages electronically via email to Susan Ellis at susan.k.ellis@usace.army.mil and copy Nicholas Lizotte at nicholas.lizotte@usace.army.mil. The capability statement must be submitted not later than 23 NOV 2026 by 2:00 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST). This Sources Sought should not be construed in any manner to be an obligation of USACE, Norfolk District to issue a contract, or result in any claim for reimbursement of costs for any effort you expend responding to this request. All information submitted will be considered procurement sensitive and is being used as a market research tool only. No solicitation is currently available. All prospective contractors are required to be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database prior to proposal submission and award. Offerors and contractors may obtain information on registration and annual confirmation requirements by calling 1-866-606-8220 or via the Internet at https://www.SAM.gov. Representations and Certifications Applications apply to this solicitation. Representations and Certifications may be completed online via SAM.gov. The Point of Contact for this requirement is Susan Ellis at susan.k.ellis@usace.army.mil, and Nicholas Lizotte at nicholas.lizotte@usace.army.mil. TELEPHONE INQUIRES WILL NOT BE HONORED.

title: FCI MCKEAN GREASE TRAP PUMPING AND CLEANING SERVICES
description: **AMMENDMENT 1. REMOVED INCORRECT WAGE DETERMINATION AND UPLOADED CORRECT WAGE DETERMINATION*** **AMMENDMENT 2. UPLOADED AMENDMENT DOCUMENT 15B20927Q00000001 P00001 RFQ GREASE TRAP.pdf THIS DOCUMENT UPDATES THE OPTION YEARS IN LINE ITEMS 2 THROUGH 5. TO BEGIN ON OCTOBER 1 INSTEAD OF DECEMBER. UPDATED TERMS AND CONDITIONS. ADDED 52.217-9 AND REMOVED 52.226-3. **** **AMMENDMENT 3. UPLOADED 15B20927Q00000001 P00002 RFQ GREASE TRAP.pdf.ALSO UPLOADED A WORD DOCUMENT WITH ALL QUESTIONS AND ANSWERS I HAVE RECEIVED RELATED TO THIS SOLICITATION. FILLED IN GOVERNMENT FILL INS, UPDATED MONTHS ON EACH CLIN TO REFLECT ACCURATE QUARTERS. ADDED LINE ITEM 6 FOR A PREDETERMINED TRIP FEE. ***** The Federal Bureau of Prisons intends to establish a contract for the provision of Grease Trap Cleaning Services. Services are to be performed on-site at FCI McKean. Place of Performance Place of Performance will be located at FCI McKean, 6975 Route 59 Lewis Run, PA 16738. Schedule The contractor will provide grease trap cleaning and waste disposal at the scheduled times below. The specific days for performance of these services will be established after contract award. The contractor will be required to provide these services on an estimated two to three month interval between the hours of 7:30AM-3:00PM, Monday through Friday, excluding Federal holidays. The exact intervals between cleanings will be determined as needed by the Contracting Officer�s Representative (COR). FCI McKean has one 10,000 gallon trap within the secure confines behind the Food Service department, and one 2,000 gallon trap at the satellite prison camp. All grease and pumpings removed shall be disposed of in accordance with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations. The contractor shall furnish an invoice for each service delivered at the time of extraction. All extractions and cleanings will be verified and signed for by an authorized representative. Specific Requirements The contractor will be licensed/permitted by the State of Pennsylvania and will provide evidence of proper waste disposal, in accordance with all current Federal, State, and local codes, laws, and requirements regarding the disposal of solid waste. Supplies and Equipment The contractor will provide the truck, labor, and equipment necessary for effective removal, transportation/disposal of waste. All material located within the container upon removal become the property and responsibility of the contractor to dispose of in a lawful manner. Description of Duties The contractor has sole responsibility and discretion for choosing and implementing the manner and method of performing tasks outlined in the Statement of Work as long as the requirements are met in accordance with the policies described above. The services, although not directly supervised, shall be reviewed by institution staff to ensure contract compliance. Contractor performance will be monitored by the COR and evaluated in accordance with FAR Part 42. Institution Security The contractor agrees to adhere to all regulations prescribed by the institution for the safety, custody, and conduct of inmates. Access to the containers will be available only during the scheduled hours, unless prior approval of the COR is obtained. All contract personnel that are entering the secure confines of the institution are required to have a clear NCIC background check.While on institution grounds and prior to departure, the operator, equipment, and vehicle shall be subject to security checks and inspections. The Government reserves the right for security reasons to prohibit certain vendor employees from entering the facility. Due to the nature of the correctional setting, delays in performance of work may be expected. Such delays may include but are not limited to inclement weather, electrical or mechanical problems, or other security matters. When the contractor reports to the institution on a scheduled pickup but is unable to performance services due to such delays, the contractor will be paid for their time in the form of a predetermined trip fee. The unperformed pickup may be rescheduled at the BOP�s discretion or may be performed on the next regularly scheduled pickup. Charges for the trip fee should be represented as separate line item charges on each invoice. The point of contact for all information regarding this solicitation is Matthew Morris, PPS, at the address listed below and telephone number (814) 362-8900, extension 3420 and/or Alyssa Mcgrew at (814)362 8900 extension 3422. Offers are due no later than November 23, 2026 at 2:00PM EST. Completed offers must be emailed to m4morris@bop.gov and amcgrew@bop.gov or faxed to (814) 363-6815. Emails are preferred. If you do not receive a confirmation email, please call to verify. The anticipated award date is December 4, 2026.
